=== passoff/1-plan-sprint-3-oidc-sign-in-spec-sub-issues-and.md
# 1. Plan Sprint 3: OIDC sign-in spec, sub-issues and an end-to-end slice

*Written 2026-11-09. The customer (course staff) assigned issue #131 for Sprints 3 and 4 on Zulip; Sprint 3 ends 2026-11-19 and needs an end-to-end demo. This prompt banks what one session already read so the next one starts at the decisions, not the discovery.*

**Model: Default (Opus 5.5). Lane: planning / spec. Waits on nothing.** This is a scope and design task with security weight (account linking). It writes documents and drafts, not product code. If it reaches the account-linking rule, hand that one path to a narrow Deep (Fable 5.1) review rather than raising the whole task. No worktree needed: it writes only under `specs/` and `docs/sprint3/`.

---

## Orientation

You are picking up for Zachary Short (GitHub `zach-short`), one of six students on team "The Calendars" in CSCI-435 at a university. The repo is the team's fork of Cal.diy (self-hosted Cal.com): `CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy`, default branch `main`. The team works in a shared repo with PR review.

Read, in this order:

1. Issue #131: `gh issue view 131 --repo CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy --comments`. It is the customer's starting spec.
2. `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root and `agents/rules/` (repository pattern, DI, `select` not `include`, no `as any`, i18n for every UI string, PR < 500 lines / < 10 files).
3. `specs/README.md` and `specs/_templates/`. Specs live in `specs/<feature>/` (design.md, decisions.md, implementation.md, future-work.md).
4. `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (whole file; the sign-in and jwt callbacks are the core of this feature), then `identityProviders.ts` beside it.
5. Issue #130 as an example of the spec depth this team ships (story, scenario, numbered acceptance criteria, out of scope).

Session rules (restated here, because this prompt is pasted alone):

- Talk to Zachary in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: short sentences, active voice, one instruction per sentence, no idioms. Documents you write keep normal project style.
- Never add a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer or a "Generated with" line to any commit or PR.
- **Never create a GitHub release or tag.** In Sprint 2 an agent created a release from this account; a teammate had to delete it, because the course grades the release snapshot the team makes at the deadline.
- Posting to GitHub (issue comments, new issues, PRs) or Zulip is outward-facing. Draft it in a file, show Zachary, and post only on his clear yes.
- Do not change `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` without asking first (project rule).
- Run `yarn type-check:ci --force` and `TZ=UTC yarn test` before any push.

## Why this exists

Organizations that self-host Cal.diy have their own identity provider (Keycloak, Authentik, Okta). Today their staff need a separate Cal.diy password. The customer wants an admin to connect any OIDC provider from the admin settings page, with no env-var change and no restart, and users to see "Continue with <provider>" on the login page. The grade depends on spec quality as much as code: the customer said explicitly that specs must cover failure, conflict, permission and old-data cases, and that open questions go to them, not to guesswork. Sprint 3 must end with one thin slice that works from the UI to the server, not disconnected parts.

## What is fixed

Read these before changing anything; do not relitigate them.

**Customer instructions (Oscar Chaparro, Zulip, after Sprint 2):**
1. Complete the spec: answer the open questions, find the ones not listed, cover failures.
2. Split #131 into sub-issues that cover the issue's areas: provider configuration (admin), login and sign-up flow, account creation and linking, user account settings, test setup.
3. Post the breakdown as a comment on #131. Each sub-issue has one owner, a full spec, and a spec review.
4. By 2026-11-19, demo a working part end to end. Out of scope per #131: SAML changes, single logout.
5. "Don't guess; ask" — on the issue or on Zulip.

**Course process rules (learned the hard way in Sprints 1–2):**
- Every issue has exactly one GitHub assignee. The **assignee (implementer)** writes or refines the spec before code, not the issue's author.
- A teammate posts a spec-review comment on the issue before implementation.
- Design decisions must name at least two concrete alternatives and why one won. "We decided X" alone loses credit.
- Nobody reviews their own PR; the reviewer posts a comment using the PR review rubric, and the reviewer merges.
- Each student reviews at least one PR per sprint and every teammate at least once over the semester.
- Each implemented issue gets a class and a sequence diagram (Mermaid is the team's tool) in `docs/sprintN/diagrams/<issue>-<login>-{class,sequence}.{mmd,png}` plus `<issue>-<login>.md`.
- AI usage logs go in `ai-logs/sprintN/<login>/`; mid-sprint check-ins in `docs/sprintN/checkin/<login>.md`. Sprint 3 folders are empty now.
- Sprint 3 milestone is #3 on GitHub, due 2026-11-19. It holds only #130 today.

**Team (GitHub login):** Zachary Short `zach-short`, Zach Bowden `zachbowden`, Dylan Han `dchan01-wm`, Joshua Ko `kojoshuay`, Julissa Hernandez `julissaehp`, Demir Beynam `dbbeynam` (still enrolled per the professor; low activity). Zach Bowden cannot run the Next.js dev server locally (it uses ~10 GB RAM and is killed); do not plan a sub-issue that only he can verify in the browser.

**Code facts (verified 2026-11-09):**
- `next-auth` is 4.24.13 (`apps/web/package.json`).
- `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts` calls `NextAuth(req, res, getOptions(...))` **per request**. So providers can be built per request from the database; that is how "no restart" becomes feasible. But today `providers` is a module-level array (`next-auth-options.ts` ~L320–370) and `getOptions` is synchronous; making it async or caching DB providers is a design decision to record.
- `IdentityProvider` enum in `schema.prisma` (~L367) is `CAL | GOOGLE | SAML | AZUREAD`. `User.identityProvider` + `identityProviderId` hold the link. An OIDC value needs a schema change and migration (ask first).
- `identityProviders.ts` maps NextAuth provider ids to the enum; `getIdentityProvider` returns `null` for unknown ids. In `signIn`, unknown → `/auth/error?error=unknown-provider`. In `jwt`, unknown → **falls back to `autoMergeIdentities()`** (~L594). Dynamic provider ids must be mapped, or OIDC logins hit those branches.
- `signIn` already rejects unverified email with `/auth/error?error=unverified-email` (~L870–890). Reuse it for the #131 criterion.
- Google and Azure use `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking: true` (~L325, L342). This is the account-takeover question in #131. Do not copy it to OIDC by default; any OIDC provider an admin adds can assert any email.
- Admin page precedent: `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/settings/(admin-layout)/admin/security/page.tsx` — role check `UserPermissionRole.ADMIN` in `page.tsx` (never `layout.tsx`), view in `apps/web/modules/settings/admin/`. Site-wide toggle precedent: `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide()` reads a global `Feature` flag via `getPrismaFeatureRepository()`.
- Secret storage precedent: `symmetricEncrypt` / `symmetricDecrypt` in `packages/lib/crypto.ts` with `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.
- Login buttons: `apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.tsx` (~L200, the Google button with `signIn("google")` and `useLastUsed`).
- No OIDC code exists yet (only i18n strings mention it). No local IdP exists in `docker-compose.yml`.

**Sprint 2 carryovers (open on GitHub as of 2026-11-09):**
- Sprint 2 milestone still open: #63 and #64 (recurrence, `dchan01-wm`), #50 and #52 (bookings calendar view and bulk actions, `dbbeynam`).
- #118 (63B, repeat days on the booking page, `dchan01-wm`), no milestone.
- #67 (force admins to enable 2FA) — Julissa pulled it from Sprint 2; unassigned. #68 (force all users to enable 2FA, `kojoshuay`) still open though PR #120 shipped the shared required-2FA modal; check whether it can close.
- PR #125 (waitlist, #13) was merged at the deadline after a review found three bugs: blank panel on fully booked days (`AvailableTimes.tsx` early return on empty slots), the six-hour waitlist hold shortened to ~5 min or deleted by the normal reserve/release flow, and duplicate offers on retry or concurrent tasks. Zach Bowden pushed fixes, but they were not re-verified. Treat them as unconfirmed until a test proves each fixed.
- #130 (`zach-short`) is already in the Sprint 3 milestone.

## Do these, in order

1. **Confirm the ground truth is still current.** Re-run `gh issue view 131 --comments`, `gh issue list --milestone "Sprint 3"`, and `git log --oneline -15 origin/main`. Teammates may have posted a breakdown or claimed sub-issues since 2026-11-09; if so, build on theirs instead of writing a rival one.
2. **Write the feature spec** at `specs/oidc-sign-in/` from the templates. In `design.md`: user story, scenario, and numbered acceptance criteria that cover the main path plus invalid provider config, provider down or slow, discovery URL unreachable, bad client secret, unverified or missing email, email that matches an existing account, provider removed while users depend on it, user whose only login is OIDC, admin who disables password login and locks themselves out, upgrade with existing users and no providers, and two providers asserting the same email. For each #131 open question, write a proposed answer **and** mark it "needs customer confirmation". In `decisions.md`: each decision with at least two alternatives (for example: DB-backed providers loaded per request vs cached with invalidation; new `OIDC` enum value plus a provider-id column vs one enum value per provider; auto-link on verified email vs reject-and-require-link-from-settings vs link only for allow-listed domains).
3. **Draft the questions for the customer** in `specs/oidc-sign-in/customer-questions.md`, short and numbered, ready to paste on #131. The account-linking rule and who may self-register are the two that block implementation.
4. **Draft the sub-issue breakdown** in `specs/oidc-sign-in/breakdown.md`: one sub-issue per area #131 lists, each with a one-paragraph spec seed, size, dependencies, and a suggested owner left blank for the team to fill. Each sub-issue must fit in one PR under 500 lines.
5. **Propose the Sprint 3 slice.** The thinnest end-to-end path: an admin adds one provider in admin settings (stored with an encrypted secret), the login page shows its button, a user signs in against a local Keycloak, a new account is created on verified email, and an unverified email shows the error. Name which sub-issues it needs and in what merge order. Anything not on that path goes to Sprint 4.
6. **List the carryovers** in `docs/sprint3/carryovers.md` with owner and a one-line next step each, so the sprint report's carryover section writes itself.
7. **Show Zachary the drafts**, then stop. Posting the breakdown on #131, creating sub-issues, and assigning owners are team actions; do them only on his explicit yes, one action at a time.

## Ask before building

- **owner's call** — Which sub-issue does Zachary own himself? He also owns #130 this sprint; the load is his call.
- **owner's call** — The account-linking rule (auto-link, reject, or domain allow-list) is the customer's decision. Propose; do not pick. The team may also choose to ask the customer before any spec review.
- **owner's call** — Whether to add a Keycloak service to `docker-compose.yml` (a shared file every teammate runs) or keep the test IdP in a separate compose file under `specs/oidc-sign-in/`.
- **owner's call** — Whether the schema change (new enum value, provider table) lands as its own first PR. It touches `schema.prisma`, which needs a yes first.

Either answer to each may be no.

## Not in scope, whoever asks

- Writing product code for OIDC in this session. This is the spec and plan; the build is a later item per sub-issue.
- SAML changes and single logout (excluded by #131).
- Changing Google or Azure login behaviour, including their `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking`.
- Mapping provider groups to Cal.diy roles beyond writing the question and a proposed answer.
- Fixing carryover bugs (waitlist, recurrence, 2FA). List them; do not fix them here.
- The Mermaid tool-showcase video and brochure.
- Creating releases or tags, merging anyone's PR, or approving reviews.

## Out of scope

BODY:
Closes #130

## What this does

The away panel for a partial-day out-of-office entry now prints the hours of the entry, for example "Away 9:00am to 10:00am". The hours are in the time zone and the 12-hour or 24-hour format selected on the booking page. Two entries that touch now give two panels. Before this change they gave one panel that showed only the first entry, so the second entry's note and redirect were lost.

## Design

**How the window reaches the panel.** `slots.ts` already copies the entry's data onto each away slot. It now also copies the window's ISO start and end into two optional fields, `outOfOfficeStart` and `outOfOfficeEnd`. Only a window has a `start`, so the fields are set behind a `"start" in` check and the slots of a whole-day entry get neither. `findOutOfOfficeForSlot` now declares that it can return an `IOutOfOfficeWindow`, which is what it returned at runtime already. The date record's top-level copy of the first window (`getUserAvailability.ts`, `acc[date] = { ...entryData, windows: [record] }`) is built from the entry data alone, so it has no `start` and cannot put the fields on another slot.

Two alternatives were rejected in the issue. A per-date list of windows beside the slots adds a new response shape that every consumer must join to the slots. Working out the hours in the booker from the first and last away slot shows slot times, which fails criterion 2.

**Where one panel ends and the next starts.** `AvailableTimes` starts a new panel when the slot's `outOfOfficeStart` or `outOfOfficeEnd` differs from the previous away slot. The same rule decides the all-away layout: when every slot is away for the same window (or for a whole-day entry, where both fields are absent), the day keeps the single whole-day panel. When two windows cover the day, the day goes through the normal list and gets one panel per window. Comparing reason and note was rejected because two entries with the same reason would merge. One panel that lists every window was rejected because a panel has one redirect button.

**The formatter.** `formatAwayWindow(startIso, endIso, timeZone, timeFormat, locale)` in `apps/web/modules/bookings/lib/formatAwayWindow.ts` is a pure function. It uses Day.js for the times because the result depends on the zone's offset at each instant, and it uses the same format strings as the slot buttons (`h:mma`, `HH:mm`). When the two instants are on different dates in the booker's zone, each time gets its date from `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with the booker's locale (month short, day numeric), for example "Oct 8, 22:00" in `en` and "8 Oct, 22:00" in `en-GB`. A window that ends exactly at the booker's midnight counts as two dates, because midnight is the first instant of the next date.

**The 12-hour and 24-hour toggle.** `AvailableTimeSlots` hid the toggle on a day where every slot is away. A day covered by windows now prints hours, so the toggle stays. It is hidden only when every slot is away and no panel has hours (`dayPrintsNoTimes`).

**Types.** `SlotInfo` (`packages/features/calendars/lib/types.ts`) and the booker's slot type (`IGetAvailableSlots` in `useAvailableTimeSlots.ts`, which is the declared return type of the tRPC schedule query) both list `notes`, `outOfOfficeStart` and `outOfOfficeEnd`. `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` no longer widens the type locally.

## Changes from the spec, after the review on #130

- The fields are named `outOfOfficeStart` and `outOfOfficeEnd` (review problem 4).
- Criterion 7 is narrowed. API v2 `2024-09-04` filters away slots out, so its responses do not change. API v2 `2024-04-15` with no `slotFormat` and no `timeZone` returns slots unchanged, so away slots there now carry the two new fields. The fields are optional and additive, which `agents/rules/api-no-breaking-changes.md` allows, so this PR does not strip them (review problem 2).
- Criterion 9 (removing `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges`) is out of this PR. It moved to a separate hardening issue so this PR stays inside the size limit. The function and its tests are unchanged here.
- A window that crosses the attendee's midnight appears on both days with the full hours and the dates. This is now tested (criterion 3).

## Out of scope

- A booked time inside a window splits the window into two panels with the same hours. `mergeByTime` puts the booked time between the away slots. This behavior comes from #104.
- Embeds render `AvailableTimes` (`Embed.tsx:416`), so they show the hours too.
- Team events, a discriminated union for `IOutOfOfficeData`, the platform atoms (their `SlotInfo` is unchanged and `OOOSlot` renders nothing there), the redirect switch in the form, and overlap rules on the server.
- Entries that overlap. Each slot still goes to the first window that matches, and each panel shows its own window's hours, so two ranges can overlap on screen.

## Tech Debt

- The weekly view (`apps/web/modules/calendars/weeklyview/components/event/Empty.tsx`) also renders `OutOfOfficeInSlots` and does not pass the hours. Its panel is unchanged.
- The discrimination between a window and a whole-day record is a `"start" in` check on a union. A discriminated union for `IOutOfOfficeData` would make it explicit, and the issue leaves that out because it changes every reader of the map.
- `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` still has no caller outside its tests. Its removal is tracked in the separate hardening issue.
- Only `en/common.json` has `ooo_away_window`. Other locales fall back to English until they are translated, and the word order "start to end" is fixed by that string.
- The date beside a time has no weekday and no year. An entry longer than a year would be ambiguous.
- The panel does not name the time zone. The booking page shows the selected zone.
- An entry whose end is set to 23:59 is stored as 23:59:59.999 (`outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts:42-45`), so the panel prints "to 23:59" (for a New York attendee of a London host, "to 6:59pm"). That matches what the host picked, but no test covers it.

## Test Evidence

Expected values come from the criterion text, the user scenario in #130 or the review discussion on #130, and from UTC offsets worked out by hand (written as comments beside each case). None was copied from the code's output.

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: hours in the booker's time zone and 12-hour or 24-hour format; changing either one updates the panel | `formatAwayWindow.test.ts` › "shows the hours in the attendee's zone, not the host's", "shows the host's own hours when the attendee is in the host's zone", "follows the 12-hour or 24-hour format for the same zone", "uses a zone with a half-hour offset", and the three "daylight saving time" cases. `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` › "shows the hours in the attendee's zone and 12-hour format", "updates the hours when the attendee changes the zone or the format". `formatAwayWindow.test.ts` › `dayPrintsNoTimes` cases (the toggle stays when a panel has hours) | unit | User scenario in #130 (London 14:00 to 15:00 is 9:00am to 10:00am in New York); UTC offsets by hand; review problem 1 on #130 |
| AC2: the window's real times, not slot times | `formatAwayWindow.test.ts` › "shows the minutes of the window, not a rounded slot time". `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` › "shows the window's real times, not the times of the slots it marks". `slots.test.ts` › "carries the window's own start and end, not the slot's, on the slot a window marks" | unit | AC text (14:10 to 14:50 with 30-minute slots) |
| AC3: the date with each time when start and end are on different dates in the attendee's zone | `formatAwayWindow.test.ts` › "adds the date to both times for an entry that spans several days", "adds the date when the window crosses midnight only for the attendee", "adds no date when the window crosses midnight for the host but not for the attendee", "takes the date from the attendee's zone, not from UTC", "keeps the 12-hour format beside the date", "writes the date the way the booker's locale does", "adds the date when the window ends exactly at the attendee's midnight", "adds the date across a month and a year". `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` › "shows the full hours with dates on both days when the window crosses the attendee's midnight". `slots.test.ts` › "carries the full start and end of an entry that spans several days on each day's slots" | unit | AC text; review comment on #130 (both days, full hours) and the answer that the date follows the booker's locale; CLDR short date order for `en`, `en-GB` and `de` |
| AC4: two back-to-back entries give two panels, each with its own note, redirect and hours; also with a gap shorter than one slot | `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` › "renders one panel for each of two back-to-back entries, with its own note, redirect and hours" (failed before the fix with "expected length 2 but got 1"), "renders two panels when the gap between two entries is shorter than one slot", "starts a new panel when only the end of the window differs", "keeps one panel for one window that marks several slots in a row". `slots.test.ts` › "gives each of two back-to-back windows its own start and end", "gives each window its own start and end when the gap between them is shorter than one slot" | unit | User scenario in #130 (Doctor, then Travel); AC text |

| AC6: whole-day entries and holidays show no hours | `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` › "shows no hours for a whole-day entry", "shows no hours on a holiday panel", "renders only the panel when every slot is away, as a whole-day entry does" (unchanged). `slots.test.ts` › "puts no start or end on the slots of a whole-day entry" | unit | AC text |
| AC7: away slots stay unbookable; API v2 `2024-09-04` responses do not change; `2024-04-15` gains two optional fields | `slots.test.ts` › every new case asserts `away: true` on the marked slots. `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` › the all-away cases assert no `time` button. API v2: see "Not tested automatically" | unit | AC text; review problem 2 on #130 |
| AC8: `SlotInfo` and the booker's slot type list `notes` and the two fields; the test no longer widens the type | `yarn type-check:ci --force` passes (9 of 9 tasks) with `type Slot = Slots[string][number]` in `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` and with tests that set `notes`, `outOfOfficeStart` and `outOfOfficeEnd` on it | type check | AC text; review problem 3 on #130 |

### Not tested automatically, and why

- **How the panel reads in the browser.** The unit tests check the text and the order of the panels, not the spacing or the look of two panels in one day. This needs a manual walk with two back-to-back entries and the booking page set to another time zone.
- **The locale passed to the formatter.** `AvailableTimes.tsx` passes `i18n.language` to `formatAwayWindow`. The test mock always returns `en`, so a wrong locale source would still pass. The formatter's own tests cover `en`, `en-GB` and `de`.
- **The join from a stored entry to the slot fields.** The engine tests start from windows built by hand, and the formatter tests start from ISO instants. No single unit test goes from an entry stored in the host's zone through `getUserAvailability` to the slot fields. The join (`getUserAvailability.ts:828-832`) was read, and the manual walk in two zones checks it.
- **API v2 responses.** The API v2 suites need a database and did not run here. The claim for `2024-09-04` (away slots filtered) and for `2024-04-15` (slots returned unchanged) comes from reading `slots-output.service.ts` in each version, as the review on #130 did.
- **End-to-end booking of an away slot.** No E2E run. The booking path is unchanged by this PR; only optional fields were added to the slot data.

### Mutation testing (D6)

StrykerJS 10.1.1 mutated only the lines this PR changed. The score went from 82.67% to 98.67% (62 to 74 killed out of the same 75 mutants). Write-up and reports: `docs/sprint3/mutation/130-zach-short.md`. The shared `stryker.config.mjs` and the two Stryker dev dependencies come from @zachbowden's PR #140, unchanged. Whichever of #140 and this PR merges second needs a `yarn.lock` merge.

The 7 surviving test gaps and 5 uncovered mutants are now killed by 10 new tests: 5 in `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` (two overlapping entries with the same end, the whole-day layout taken from `main`, a day with no away entry, the last panel's padding, the redirect date across midnight UTC) and 5 in the new `AvailableTimeSlots.test.tsx` (the time format toggle, which no test rendered before). One mutant (`AvailableTimes.tsx:370`, `&&` to `||`) is equivalent: `slots.ts` sets both window fields or neither.

### AI-written tests

All 47 new tests in this PR were written by an AI agent (Claude). The first 37 came with the feature: 5 in `slots.test.ts`, 20 in `formatAwayWindow.test.ts` and 12 in `AvailableTimes.test.tsx`. They were written before the code they cover, and the 4 engine tests and 10 component tests that depend on the new behavior were run and seen to fail first. The expected values were worked out by hand from the criteria and from UTC offsets, and the working is in comments beside the cases. The harness changes in `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` (a `useBookerTime` mock that a test can change, and a `t` mock that prints the English `ooo_away_window` string) are also AI-written. The 10 mutation-testing tests above were written by Claude Code against the before report, and each one was confirmed in the after report to kill the mutants listed in the write-up.

## Size

Counted with tests, as the review on #130 counted: 10 code files and 616 changed lines, plus `common.json` (1 line). Without tests: 7 code files and 95 changed lines. The 500-line count is above the limit only because of the 37 new tests (521 lines in 3 test files). Criterion 9 (the dead-code removal) moved to its own issue to hold the file count at 10.

With the mutation-testing commits: 3 more code files (`stryker.130.config.mjs`, `vitest.stryker-130.config.mts` and the shared `stryker.config.mjs` from #140), 1 more test file, and 1,125 lines of `yarn.lock` for the Stryker dependencies. Without tests that is 10 code files.

BODY:
### What does this PR do?

Adds a shared StrykerJS setup for the Sprint 3 mutation testing deliverable (D6), so each of us can run the tool on the files our own PRs change. No product code changes. There is no issue for this yet; it is team tooling for D6.

### What changed

- `package.json` / `yarn.lock`: `@stryker-mutator/core` and `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.1.1 as root dev dependencies. 10.1.1 supports our Vitest 4.1.8 and needs Node 22 or later.
- `stryker.config.mjs`: Vitest runner with the root `vitest.config.mts`, `related: true` (only tests that import the mutated file run), clear-text, progress, JSON and HTML reporters. The JSON report goes to `STRYKER_JSON` if set.
- `.gitignore`: ignores the local `reports/mutation/` output and `.stryker-tmp/`.

### How to use it

Run it only on the files your PR changed:

```bash
TZ=UTC STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json yarn stryker run --mutate "path/to/changed-file.ts"
```

Then add or strengthen a test, and run again with `-after.json`. Commit both JSON reports with your D6 write-up. If you use this setup, credit it in your D6 file as the course asks.

### Design decisions

**Sandbox vs in-place.** I tried `inPlace: true` first, because the default sandbox copies the repo. In this monorepo the in-place backup lands inside the project, Vitest then collected the backup copies, and the restore dropped the executable bit on three tracked scripts. The sandbox avoids both, at the cost of a copy. The copy leaves out `docs`, `ai-logs`, `specs`, `apps/api/v2`, `apps/web/public`, `packages/embeds` and `reports` to stay small, and `.claude`, `.cursor` and `packages/prisma/.env`, because they are symlinks the copy cannot follow.

**Related tests only vs a fixed test folder.** `vitest.related` runs the tests that import the mutated file. A fixed `vitest.dir` per run would need each of us to pick the folder and risks false survivors when a covering test sits elsewhere.

### Tech Debt

* **Introduced:** Stryker's sandbox copy adds a few seconds per run. The ignore list must grow if someone adds another symlinked folder.
* **Encountered:** On Node 26, `yarn prisma generate` exits with code 1 (the Zod generator uses a removed `fs` option while it deletes old output), although it still writes every file. This also makes the root `postinstall` fail on Node 26.

### Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stryker runs on one file with only its related tests | Manual: `TZ=UTC yarn stryker run --mutate packages/features/auth/lib/identityProviders.ts` → initial run 8 tests passed; 2 mutants tested, 2 killed; done in 7 s | manual | StrykerJS docs |
| Stryker runs on a React component with jsdom tests | Manual: `--mutate apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimes.tsx` → initial run 14 tests passed; 62 killed, 122 survived, 138 no coverage (score 19.25%); done in 35 s | manual | StrykerJS docs |
| A run leaves no change in tracked files | Manual: `git status --short` after both runs shows no tracked changes | manual | course D6 (commit only the reports) |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** this PR adds tooling, not product behavior; the checks above are the tool's own runs.

**AI-written tests:** None.

BODY:
### What does this PR do?

Adds the draft spec for #131 (sign in with any OIDC provider) and the Sprint 3 carryovers list. Documentation only; no product code.

### What changed

- `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md`: user story, scenario, 43 numbered acceptance criteria (main path, provider failures, unverified or missing email, existing-account conflicts, provider removal, lock-out, upgrade), and a proposed answer for each #131 open question, marked as needing customer confirmation.
- `specs/oidc-sign-in/decisions.md`: nine decisions, each with at least two alternatives and the reason for the choice. Account linking (ADR-004) is left to the customer.
- `specs/oidc-sign-in/customer-questions.md`: 13 numbered questions to post on #131. Q1 (account linking) and Q2 (who may sign up) block implementation.
- `specs/oidc-sign-in/breakdown.md`: nine sub-issues with size, dependencies and a blank owner column, plus a comment ready to post on #131.
- `specs/oidc-sign-in/implementation.md`: the Sprint 3 slice and merge order.

A login whose email matches an existing account is rejected until the customer answers Q1. Merge order: sub-issue 1; then 3 and 5 in parallel; then 4 and 6; sub-issue 2 at any time.

=== 136
Sub-issue 1 of #131. Full feature spec: `specs/oidc-sign-in/` in PR #133. Numbers in brackets, such as [39], are acceptance criteria in `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md`.


### Is your proposal related to a problem?

#131 lets an admin add OIDC providers at run time. Today the only providers are hard-coded and configured with environment variables, and the database has no place to store a provider, its client secret, or its sign-up rules. `IdentityProvider` (`schema.prisma:367`) has no value for an OIDC user. Every other #131 sub-issue (admin backend, admin page, login flow) reads or writes this data, so it comes first.

### Describe the solution you would like

Add an `OIDC` value to `IdentityProvider` and a new `OidcProvider` table with a migration. Add `PrismaOidcProviderRepository`, wired with the moduleLoader DI pattern, that is the only code that reads or writes the table. It returns DTOs, never Prisma types. The client secret is stored only as ciphertext; encrypting it is the admin service's job (sub-issue 3), not the repository's.

### User story

As a developer on the #131 sub-issues, I want one repository for OIDC providers, so that the admin backend and the login flow read the same data in the same way and the secret cannot leak through a query that selects too much.

### User scenario

The admin service (sub-issue 3) calls `create` with an encrypted secret. The login route (sub-issue 5) calls `findEnabled` on each auth request and gets the enabled providers in display order, without their secrets, then calls `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret` for the one provider whose flow it builds. When an admin removes a provider, the service calls `deleteWithAccounts`, and the provider and every user link to it go in one transaction.

### Scope

Medium. It touches the Prisma schema and one migration, a new repository with its DTO, the DI module and container, and unit tests. I expect 6 to 8 files and about 300 changed lines, half of them tests. It adds no UI and no tRPC route.

### Acceptance criteria

1. A migration adds `OIDC` to `IdentityProvider` and creates `OidcProvider` with: `id` (cuid, primary key), `displayName` (text), `issuer` (text), `clientId` (text), `clientSecretEncrypted` (text), `scopes` (text), `allowSignup` (boolean), `allowedDomains` (text array), `enabled` (boolean), `position` (integer), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `updatedById` (nullable integer).
2. New rows get these defaults: `scopes = "openid email profile"`, `allowSignup = false`, `allowedDomains = []`, `enabled = false`, `position = 0`.
3. Two providers cannot have the same `issuer` and `clientId`. A second insert with the same pair fails with a unique-constraint error, and the repository turns it into an `ErrorWithCode` with a message that names the issuer, not the secret.
4. The migration applies to a database that already has users and accounts, and changes no existing row. `CAL`, `GOOGLE`, `SAML` and `AZUREAD` users keep their values. [39]
5. `findEnabled()` returns only enabled providers, ordered by `position` and then `createdAt`, as `OidcProviderPublicDto` (`id`, `displayName`, `issuer`, `clientId`, `scopes`, `allowSignup`, `allowedDomains`). It never selects `clientSecretEncrypted`. [6, 11]
6. `list()` returns every provider (enabled or not) in the same order and shape as criterion 5, plus `enabled`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. It never selects `clientSecretEncrypted`. [6]
7. `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret(id)` is the only method that returns `clientSecretEncrypted`. It returns `null` for an unknown id.
8. `create`, `update` and `setEnabled` write only the fields they are given. `update` without a new secret leaves `clientSecretEncrypted` unchanged. Each returns the shape of criterion 6.
9. `countLinkedAccounts(id)` returns the number of distinct users with an `Account` row whose `provider` is `oidc-<id>`. [36]
10. `deleteWithAccounts(id)` deletes the provider and every `Account` row with `provider = "oidc-<id>"` in one transaction. If either delete fails, neither happens. Deleting an unknown id throws `ErrorWithCode` not-found and deletes nothing. [37]
11. `getOidcProviderRepository()` returns the repository from the DI container, built with `bindModuleToClassOnToken` like `packages/features/credentials/di/CredentialRepository.module.ts`.
12. Every query uses `select`, never `include`. No method returns a Prisma type; the DTOs live in `packages/lib/dto/`.
13. `yarn type-check:ci --force` passes. Code that switches over `IdentityProvider` handles `OIDC` (for example the provider name on `/auth/error`, `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx:39-48`, falls back to "your original login method").
14. Unit tests with a mocked Prisma client cover criteria 3 and 5 to 10, including a check that the `select` of `findEnabled` and `list` has no `clientSecretEncrypted` key.

### Out of scope

- Encrypting or decrypting the secret, field validation, the 10-provider limit and the discovery test (sub-issue 3).
- Admin UI (sub-issue 4) and the login flow (sub-issue 5).
- Mapping `oidc-<id>` to `IdentityProvider.OIDC` in `identityProviders.ts` (sub-issue 5).
- Any change to `User` or `Account` columns. The user link is an `Account` row (ADR-002).

### Design decisions

**Where the provider order comes from.** Store an integer `position`, sorted with `createdAt` as the tie-breaker.

1. Sort by `createdAt` only. Rejected: the admin cannot put the main provider first (design criterion 11 asks for an admin-set order).
2. A linked list (`previousId`). Rejected: reordering needs several row updates and is easy to corrupt; 10 rows at most do not need it.

**How `allowedDomains` is stored.** A Postgres text array on the provider row.

1. A separate `OidcProviderDomain` table. Rejected: a second table and a join for at most a handful of strings that are always read with the provider.
2. One comma-separated text column. Rejected: the code must split and trim it everywhere, and a domain with a stray space would not match.

**How a user is linked to a provider.** Use the existing `Account` table with `provider = "oidc-<id>"`, not a new column on `User`. See ADR-002 in `specs/oidc-sign-in/decisions.md`: `Account` already has `@@unique([provider, providerAccountId])` (`schema.prisma:1258`), and a column on `User` would allow only one link per user.

**Who records the last editor.** `updatedById` is a plain nullable integer, not a relation to `User`.

1. A relation to `User`. Rejected: it changes the `User` model, which every Cal.diy query touches, for an audit field nobody joins on.
2. No editor field. Rejected: when two admins edit one provider (design criterion 8), the page cannot say who saved last.

### Technical notes

- Repository pattern: `packages/features/selectedSlots/repositories/PrismaSelectedSlotRepository.ts` (constructor takes `PrismaClient`).
- DI pattern: `packages/features/credentials/di/CredentialRepository.module.ts`; tokens in a new `packages/features/auth/oidc/di/tokens.ts`, spread into `packages/features/di/tokens.ts`.
- Migration folder name: `<timestamp>_add_oidc_provider` in `packages/prisma/migrations/`, after `20261029130000_add_waitlist_entry_slot_start`.
- Run `yarn prisma generate` after the schema change.
- Likely files: `schema.prisma`, the migration, `PrismaOidcProviderRepository.ts` and its test, `packages/lib/dto/OidcProviderDto.ts`, `OidcProviderRepository.module.ts`, `OidcProviderRepository.container.ts`, `tokens.ts` (two files), and `auth/error/page.tsx` if criterion 13 needs it.

### Mutation testing

The repository methods are short and have clear branches (unknown id, unchanged secret, transaction rollback), so StrykerJS can run on `PrismaOidcProviderRepository.ts` with only its own test file.

Hi @all,

This is your team's feature for Sprints 3 and 4.

A few things you should consider:

1. Complete the spec. The issue is a starting point: the acceptance criteria are incomplete and the open questions need answers. We expect thorough specs that cover what happens when things go wrong (invalid input, failures, conflicts, permissions, old data), not only the main path. The open questions are not a complete list; find the other cases too.
2. Given the scope of the issue, split the feature into sub-issues. Your breakdown should cover the areas listed in the issue.
3. Plan which sub-issues go in Sprint 3. Post your breakdown as a comment on the issue. Each sub-issue should have an owner, a full spec, and a spec review.
4. By the end of Sprint 3 (Nov 19), deliver a working part of the feature that we can demo end-to-end, from the UI to the server. It doesn't need to be complete, but it must work as a whole, not as separate pieces that aren't connected yet.

Treat us as your customer. If anything is unclear or you need a decision about the expected behavior, ask us on the issue or on Zulip. Don't guess; ask.

Cheers,
--- zach-short 2026-11-11T20:08:45Z
hi @ojcchar, a few questions on #131 before we finish the spec. we put what we'd do next to each one, just tell us if that's fine or what you want instead. 1 and 2 block us.

1. if someone logs in with oidc and their email already has a cal.diy account, what should happen? we think auto link only if the admin says the provider owns that email domain, otherwise reject and make them link it from settings. never auto link an admin account.
2. who can make a new account through oidc? we think a per provider "allow new accounts" switch (off by default) plus an optional list of allowed domains. should the existing "disable signup" setting block oidc signup too?
3. if the provider doesn't send email_verified, we reject the login. ok?
4. do you want a switch to turn off password login? if so admins would always keep password login so nobody gets locked out. we'd do this in sprint 4.
5. if an admin removes a provider people use, we show how many users it affects, make them type the name to confirm, and those users can use forgot password to get back in. ok?
6. should the require 2fa setting apply to oidc users too, or does the provider's mfa count?
7. if someone's email changes at the provider, we update it in cal.diy if it's verified and not taken. ok?
8. if someone was invited but hasn't accepted yet, should an oidc login with that email take over the invite, or treat it like 1?
9. no mapping provider groups to cal.diy roles for now. ok?
10. users can unlink a provider unless it's their only way to log in. ok?
11. is up to 10 providers enough?
12. we're testing with keycloak locally. is that ok or do you want authentik or okta too?
13. after upgrading nothing changes until an admin adds a provider. ok?

thanks!

--- ojcchar 2026-11-12T19:28:06Z
These are good questions, and your proposals are mostly what we want.

1. Agreed: auto-link only when the email is verified and the admin marked the provider as owning that domain. Otherwise reject and let the user link it from settings. Never auto-link admin accounts.
2. Agreed on the per-provider switch (off by default) and the allowed domains. Yes, the global "disable signup" setting also blocks OIDC sign-up, and it wins over the provider switch. An admin who turned off sign-up expects no new accounts from anywhere. They can still let people in by inviting them (see 8).
3. Yes, reject the login if email_verified is missing or false.
4. Yes, in Sprint 4. Admins always keep password login.
5. Fine, but check one thing: users created through OIDC have no password, so make sure "forgot password" actually works for them, and test it. Also let admins disable a provider instead of deleting it.
6. We'd like users to rely on the provider's MFA when it can be checked. Add a per-provider setting, "accept this provider's MFA." When it's on and the ID token's amr claim shows a second factor, skip Cal.diy's 2FA. If amr is missing or shows only a password, require Cal.diy's 2FA. This can be in Sprint 4.
7. Fine, as long as accounts are matched by the provider's user ID (the sub claim), never by email. If the new email is already taken, keep the old one and tell the user.
8. A verified OIDC login with an invited email accepts the invite, even if "allow new accounts" is off for that provider.
9. Agreed, no group mapping for now.
10. Agreed.
11. Yes, 10 is enough.
12. Keycloak is fine. Document the setup so anyone on the team can run the tests.
13. Agreed.

author:	dchan01-wm
association:	collaborator
edited:	false
status:	none
--
## Spec Review — @dchan01-wm

Claude helped me with this; overall the spec seems good, there are a couple issues it identified (I did not extensively look into them, but you can use this as a starting point) but you should be good to go!

- **AC1:** testable, but see problem 1: on a day where every slot is away, the 12h/24h toggle is hidden, so "changing either one updates the panel" cannot be done from that day.
- **AC2:** clear and testable; the 14:10–14:50 example with 30-minute slots pins down "real times, not slot times" well.
- **AC3:** testable, but the date format is not stated (e.g. "Wed, Nov 12, 9:00pm" vs "11/12 21:00"). Please name it, or say it follows the booker's locale, so a test has an expected value that does not come from the code's own output.
- **AC4:** clear and testable, including the shorter-than-one-slot gap.
- **AC5:** clear, but interacts with problem 1 (both cases make the day "all away").
- **AC6:** clear and testable.
- **AC7:** "unbookable" is testable; "API v2 slot responses do not change" is not true as written (problem 2).
- **AC8:** testable by type-check, but incomplete (problem 3).
- **AC9:** testable, but it is a cleanup that the user story does not need (see Scope).

**Cases considered:** Covered: one window in the host's and another zone (AC1), slot-straddling edges (AC2), multi-day partial entries (AC5), back-to-back entries (AC4), whole-day entries and holidays (AC6). Overlapping entries and platform atoms are out of scope; fine.

Worth adding:
- **Window crossing the attendee's midnight:** slots are grouped by the attendee's date (`util.ts:1278`), so the panel appears on both days with the full hours. Probably right; say so in AC3 so it gets a test.
- **A booked time inside a window:** `mergeByTime` puts it between the away slots (`AvailableTimes.tsx:281-303`), splitting one window into two panels with the same hours. Pre-existing from #104; add it to Out of Scope or skip booked times in the boundary rule.
- **Embeds** also render `AvailableTimes` (`Embed.tsx:416`), so they get the hours too. Fine; worth a line.

**Scope:** Medium fits. The file list is already 10 code files plus `common.json`, and problems 1 and 3 add one or two more, which is over the 10-file PR limit (`AGENTS.md`). Suggest moving AC9 (deleting `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges`, now used only by its tests: `date-ranges.ts:279`, `date-ranges.test.ts:1297-1376`) into its own small hardening issue.

**Problems found:** 

1. **12h/24h toggle hidden on all-away days.** `AvailableTimeSlots.tsx:206` and `:216` hide it when every slot is away, which conflicts with AC1 on AC5's days. Either show it when a panel has hours (add `AvailableTimeSlots.tsx` to the file list) or narrow AC1.
2. **AC7 is false for API v2 2024-04-15.** 2024-09-04 filters away slots (`slots-output.service.ts:49`, `:119`), but 2024-04-15 with no `slotFormat` and no `timeZone` returns slots unchanged (`slots-2024-04-15/services/slots-output.service.ts:25-26`), so the new fields would appear there. That is additive, so not breaking (`agents/rules/api-no-breaking-changes.md`), but the AC should say so, or the PR should strip them.
3. **AC8 misses the booker's type.** `AvailableTimes.tsx:21` uses `Slot`, which comes from `IGetAvailableSlots` (`useAvailableTimeSlots.ts:7-21`), not `SlotInfo`. Add the new fields (and `notes`) there and name the file.
4. **Name the two new fields** (e.g. `outOfOfficeStart` / `outOfOfficeEnd`).
5. Optional: `findOutOfOfficeForSlot`'s return type (`slots.ts:13`, `:20`) has no `start`/`end` and needs widening.

Everything else in the technical notes matches the code (`slots.ts:16-25`, `:245-258`; `getUserAvailability.ts:229-232`; `AvailableTimes.tsx:272-306`; `util.ts:1275-1290`; `outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts:152-161`). The design is feasible, and both decisions have two well-argued alternatives.
--

===
name: Install playwright binaries
description: "Install playwright, cache and restore if necessary"
inputs:
  skip-install-if-cache-hit:
    description: "Skip playwright install if cache is hit. Use this for jobs that only need to check that cache exists."
    required: false
    default: "false"
runs:
  using: "composite"
  steps:
    - name: Get installed Playwright version
      shell: bash
      id: playwright-version
      run: echo "PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION=$(node -e "console.log(require('./package.json').devDependencies['@playwright/test'])")" >> $GITHUB_ENV

    # When skip-install-if-cache-hit is true, first check if cache exists without downloading (lookup-only mode)
    - name: Check playwright cache (lookup-only)
      if: ${{ inputs.skip-install-if-cache-hit == 'true' }}
      id: playwright-cache-check
      uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
      with:
        path: |
          ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright
          ~/.cache/ms-playwright
          ${{ github.workspace }}/node_modules/playwright
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-playwright-${{ env.PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION }}
        lookup-only: true

    # Only restore cache if not in skip mode, or if skip mode but cache check missed
    - name: Cache playwright binaries
      if: ${{ inputs.skip-install-if-cache-hit != 'true' || steps.playwright-cache-check.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' }}
      id: playwright-cache
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: |
          ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright
          ~/.cache/ms-playwright
          ${{ github.workspace }}/node_modules/playwright
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-playwright-${{ env.PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION }}

    # In default mode: run if playwright-cache missed
    # In skip mode: run if playwright-cache-check missed (but cache restore step was also skipped)
    - name: Yarn playwright install
      if: ${{ (inputs.skip-install-if-cache-hit != 'true' && steps.playwright-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true') || (inputs.skip-install-if-cache-hit == 'true' && steps.playwright-cache-check.outputs.cache-hit != 'true') }}
      shell: bash
      run: yarn playwright install --with-deps

# Sprint 3 mid-sprint check-in: zach-short

**Code PR:** TODO: link the #130 PR here before Nov 12, 11:59 PM (it must be open and ready for review, or merged).

## What have you implemented so far, and what remains?

So far my Sprint 3 work is planning. For the team feature, #131 (OIDC sign-in), I drafted the spec with 43 acceptance criteria, nine design decisions with alternatives, and a breakdown into nine sub-issues with a Sprint 3 demo slice (PR #133). I posted our questions to the customer on #131. For #130 (hours on the partial-day away panel) I wrote the build plan and a draft Test Evidence table, one row per acceptance criterion.

What remains: the #130 code PR after its spec review, my OIDC sub-issue once the team assigns owners, its spec review and PR, and mutation testing with StrykerJS on one of my issues.

## What is one thing you learned about testing in your project?

Passing tests only show that the code does what the tests expect, not what the spec asks. In Sprint 2, PR #125 (waitlist) passed all 45 existing tests, yet a review found three real bugs: a blank panel on fully booked days, a six-hour hold cut to five minutes, and duplicate offers on retry. No test had checked those cases, because the tests followed the code's main path.

So for #130 I wrote the expected values from the acceptance criteria before writing any code. For example, a 14:10 to 14:50 window must print 14:10 and 14:50, not the 14:00 and 15:00 slot times.

## What is one risk to finishing your work by Nov 19, and what will you do about it?

The biggest risk is the OIDC demo. It needs five sub-issues merged in order, and one of them changes the 1,255-line `next-auth-options.ts`, where a mistake in account linking can let one user log in as another. Every sub-issue also needs a spec review and an approval before merge, so a one-day wait at each step adds up.

To reduce this, the breakdown has a merge order so that two people can work in parallel after the first PR. The account-linking code waits for the customer's answer. Until then we reject matching emails, which is safe. I will also ask for reviews on Zulip the day each PR opens.

# #131 sub-issue breakdown (draft)

Draft for the team. After the team fills the Owner column, paste the "Comment for #131" section as a comment on #131. Then create one sub-issue per row; each owner writes the full spec in their sub-issue before code, and a teammate posts a spec review.

Full spec: `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md` (criteria numbers below refer to it). Decisions: `decisions.md`.

## Rules for every sub-issue

- One GitHub assignee, who writes or refines the sub-issue spec before code. The spec states its scope (small or medium) and one or two sentences on why.
- Link each sub-issue to #131 and attach it to the Sprint 3 milestone. Sub-issues count toward each member's two-medium-issue minimum.
- A spec-review comment from another teammate before implementation. It must say what was checked: each acceptance criterion clear and testable, which cases were considered, whether the scope fits. "Looks good" alone does not count.
- One PR under 500 changed lines and under 10 code files. The description has `Closes #<sub-issue>`, the Tech Debt section and the Test Evidence table (one row per criterion; expected values come from the criterion, never from the code's output).
- Merge only after a teammate approves the latest commit. After that approval the author may merge. Request the review on GitHub and tell the reviewer on Zulip; reviewers answer within 24 hours.
- Sprint 3 replaces UML diagrams with mutation testing (StrykerJS with the Vitest runner) on one of each member's issues. Rows 1, 3 and 5 have the most unit-testable logic for this.
- Zach Bowden cannot run the Next.js dev server. Rows 1, 3 and 5 can be verified with unit tests alone; rows 4, 6 and 8 need a browser.

## Comment for #131

---

**Breakdown of #131 into sub-issues**

Full draft spec (acceptance criteria, edge cases, proposed answers, decisions with alternatives): `specs/oidc-sign-in/` on branch `docs/oidc-spec`. Our questions for you are in the next comment.

| # | Sub-issue | Area in #131 | Size | Depends on | Sprint | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | OIDC provider data model and repository | Provider configuration | M | none | 3 | |
| 2 | Local Keycloak test provider and realm | Test setup | S | none | 3 | |
| 3 | Admin provider service and tRPC procedures | Provider configuration | M | 1 | 3 | |
| 4 | Admin "Identity providers" settings page | Provider configuration | M | 3 | 3 | |
| 5 | Load providers per request and create new OIDC users | Login and sign-up | M | 1 | 3 | |
| 6 | Login page buttons and sign-in error messages | Login and sign-up | S | 5 | 3 | |
| 7 | Link OIDC to existing accounts (rule from customer) | Account creation and linking | M | 5, customer Q1 | 4 | |
| 8 | Connected logins in Settings → Security (link, unlink) | User account settings | M | 7 | 4 | |
| 9 | Provider removal, password-login switch, end-to-end tests | Provider configuration, test setup | M | 4, 7 | 4 | |

**Sprint 3 demo (by Nov 19):** an admin adds a Keycloak provider in admin settings (secret stored encrypted), the login page shows "Continue with <name>", a user with a verified email signs in and gets a new account, and a user with an unverified email sees a clear error. A login whose email matches an existing account is rejected for now, which is safe under every answer to our linking question. Merge order: 1 first; then 3 and 5 in parallel; then 4 (after 3) and 6 (after 5). Row 2 can merge at any time.

---

## Sub-issue seeds

Each seed is the starting spec. The owner expands it into a full issue (story, scenario, numbered criteria, out of scope, design decisions with two alternatives) like #130.

### 1. OIDC provider data model and repository (M, Sprint 3)

Add `OIDC` to `enum IdentityProvider` and a new `OidcProvider` model (fields in design.md, Database Changes) with a migration. Add `PrismaOidcProviderRepository` (`findEnabled`, `findById`, `list`, `create`, `update`, `delete`, `countLinkedUsers`) using `select`, never `include`, and wire it with the moduleLoader DI pattern. The secret column stores only ciphertext. Criteria 3 (shape), 9, 39, 40. Unit tests for the repository with a mocked Prisma client. **Needs a yes before editing `schema.prisma`** (project rule). ~250 lines. Verifiable without the dev server.

### 2. Local Keycloak test provider and realm (S, Sprint 3)

Add a compose file and a realm export with one client (`cal-diy`, confidential, redirect URI `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/*`) and three users: verified email, unverified email, no email claim. Add a README with exact start and stop commands and the values to paste into the admin page. Where the compose service lives is an owner's call (ADR-008). Criterion 42. ~150 lines, mostly JSON.

### 3. Admin provider service and tRPC procedures (M, Sprint 3)

Add `OidcProviderService`: field validation (criteria 3, 4), secret encryption with `symmetricEncrypt` and a clear error when `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is bad (6, 10), and `testDiscovery` with a 5-second timeout that returns one of the results in criterion 5. Add `viewer.admin.oidcProviders.{list,create,update,setEnabled,delete,testDiscovery}` on `authedAdminProcedure`; `list` returns a DTO with no secret field (2, 6). Enabling requires a passing discovery test. Unit tests cover each validation error, each discovery result and the non-admin `FORBIDDEN` path. ~400 lines with tests. Verifiable without the dev server.

### 4. Admin "Identity providers" settings page (M, Sprint 3)

Add `settings/(admin-layout)/admin/identity-providers/page.tsx` with the `ADMIN` role check in the page, and a view in `apps/web/modules/settings/admin/`. List providers; add and edit form with inline errors; write-only secret field ("Secret is set" / "Replace secret"); callback URL with copy button; Test connection button with its result; enable and disable switch; reorder. Every string in `common.json`. Criteria 1–9. Delete with typed confirmation moves to row 9. ~400 lines. Needs a browser.

### 5. Load providers per request and create new OIDC users (M, Sprint 3)

Make the NextAuth route handler async: load enabled providers through the repository and pass them to `getOptions` as `dynamicProviders` (ADR-001). Build each as a next-auth `oauth` provider with `wellKnown`, `idToken: true`, PKCE and state, a 5-second HTTP timeout, and no dangerous email linking. Map the `oidc-` prefix to `IdentityProvider.OIDC`. Add `OidcSignInService`, called from the top of `signIn` and `jwt` (ADR-005): reject unverified (15), missing email (16), name fallback (17), sign-up rules (18), create the user and `Account` row (14), find returning users by (provider, `sub`) (19), keep TOTP (20), and reject any email match with `oidc-account-exists` (27, Sprint 3 rule). Create the user and `Account` row in one transaction; leave `identityProviderId` null. A test per branch, including criterion 28 (no path reaches the shared lookups or auto-merge code) and a two-providers-one-`sub` test (criterion 30). Rules 1–4 from the Deep review in ADR-005 apply. ~450 lines with tests. **Gets a narrow Deep review of the `signIn` and `jwt` changes before merge.** Verifiable with unit tests; the demo needs row 2.

### 6. Login page buttons and sign-in error messages (S, Sprint 3)

Pass enabled providers (id and display name only) from the login and sign-up `getServerSideProps`. Render one "Continue with <name>" button per provider after Microsoft, with `useLastUsed` (11, 12). Read `error` from the URL on the login page and show messages for `OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback` and `AccessDenied` (21–25). Add the new error codes to `/auth/error` (`missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists`, `unknown-provider`). ~200 lines. Needs a browser.

### 7. Link OIDC to existing accounts (M, Sprint 4)

Implement the customer's answer to Q1 and Q8 inside `OidcSignInService`: domain-based auto-link or reject, never for `ADMIN` accounts, invited-user rule, two providers with one email (30), email change at the provider (31). Calls `linkAccount` inside `signIn` so that next-auth finds the account by (provider, `sub`). **Gets a narrow Deep review.** Criteria 27–32. ~300 lines with tests.

### 8. Connected logins in Settings → Security (M, Sprint 4)

List linked providers with link dates (33). "Link" starts the flow for the signed-in user with `prompt=login` and adds an `Account` row to that user, with a clear error if the `sub` is linked elsewhere (34). Needs the `getSessionUserId` getter in `getOptions` (ADR-005, rule 3). "Unlink" is disabled when it is the last login method and explains the set-password flow (35). ~350 lines. Needs a browser.

### 9. Provider removal, password-login switch, end-to-end tests (M, Sprint 4)

Delete with typed confirmation and linked-user counts (36, 37), disable keeps links (38). If the customer wants it (Q4), the password-login switch with the admin break-glass rule (41). Playwright test against the Keycloak realm for criteria 14 and 15 (43). May split into two PRs if the switch is in scope. ~400 lines.
```

        releaseAt: { gt: new Date() },

## What does this PR do?

<!-- Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed. Please also include relevant motivation and context. List any dependencies that are required for this change. -->

This PR implements the new "Running Late" feature, allowing hosts to notify attendees if they are running behind schedule. It introduces a secure backend service via Dependency Injection, a Zod-validated tRPC mutation, and a frontend dialog for the booking list. The motivation is to give hosts a quick way to communicate delays (5-30 minutes) to prevent attendees from abandoning the meeting. 

- Closes #137 

## Design 
*Note: Design documentation included as per project requirements.*

*   **Decision**: The server treats a requester as a host only when their logged-in session matches the booking's organizer or one of its hosts.
*   **Alternatives considered**: 1. Reusing the existing cancellation logic which accepts a client-provided email. 2. Blocking the action entirely for everyone.
*   **Rationale**: The chosen option cannot be faked by attendees, whereas reusing the existing logic would allow an attendee to spoof the host's email and bypass the rules.
*   **Consequences**: This decision makes the feature secure against unauthorized use, but it makes it harder for hosts who are logged out, as they are blocked and must log in first to send a notice.

**Test Strategy:**
Automated unit tests were added to cover all behavioral changes, specifically focusing on authorization barriers, time window boundaries, and email payload generation. 

**Automated Tests:**
*   Run `vitest` to execute the new test suites for `isWithinRunningLateWindow` and `RunningLateService`.
*   Tests verify that the 2-hour window is strictly enforced (exactly 2 hours is accepted, 2 hours and 1 millisecond is rejected).
*   Tests confirm that requests from non-organizers and attendees are immediately rejected.
*   Tests validate that attendees are successfully deduplicated before emails are sent.

**Manual Verification:**
If CI is not yet configured for this environment, please manually verify the following:
1.  Log in as a host and navigate to the Bookings list.
2.  Locate a booking starting within the next 2 hours and verify the "Running Late" action appears.
3.  Submit a notice and verify the success toast appears. 
4.  Log in as the attendee of that same booking and verify the action button is entirely hidden.

- Are there environment variables that should be set?
No new environment variables are required for this feature.

hi @ojcchar, a few questions on #131 before we finish the spec. we put what we'd do next to each one, just tell us if that's fine or what you want instead. 1 and 2 block us.

1. if someone logs in with oidc and their email already has a cal.diy account, what should happen? we think auto link only if the admin says the provider owns that email domain, otherwise reject and make them link it from settings. never auto link an admin account.
2. who can make a new account through oidc? we think a per provider "allow new accounts" switch (off by default) plus an optional list of allowed domains. should the existing "disable signup" setting block oidc signup too?
3. if the provider doesn't send email_verified, we reject the login. ok?
4. do you want a switch to turn off password login? if so admins would always keep password login so nobody gets locked out. we'd do this in sprint 4.
5. if an admin removes a provider people use, we show how many users it affects, make them type the name to confirm, and those users can use forgot password to get back in. ok?
6. should the require 2fa setting apply to oidc users too, or does the provider's mfa count?
7. if someone's email changes at the provider, we update it in cal.diy if it's verified and not taken. ok?
8. if someone was invited but hasn't accepted yet, should an oidc login with that email take over the invite, or treat it like 1?
9. no mapping provider groups to cal.diy roles for now. ok?
10. users can unlink a provider unless it's their only way to log in. ok?
11. is up to 10 providers enough?
12. we're testing with keycloak locally. is that ok or do you want authentik or okta too?
13. after upgrading nothing changes until an admin adds a provider. ok?

thanks!

These are good questions, and your proposals are mostly what we want.

1. Agreed: auto-link only when the email is verified and the admin marked the provider as owning that domain. Otherwise reject and let the user link it from settings. Never auto-link admin accounts.
2. Agreed on the per-provider switch (off by default) and the allowed domains. Yes, the global "disable signup" setting also blocks OIDC sign-up, and it wins over the provider switch. An admin who turned off sign-up expects no new accounts from anywhere. They can still let people in by inviting them (see 8).
3. Yes, reject the login if email_verified is missing or false.
4. Yes, in Sprint 4. Admins always keep password login.
5. Fine, but check one thing: users created through OIDC have no password, so make sure "forgot password" actually works for them, and test it. Also let admins disable a provider instead of deleting it.
6. We'd like users to rely on the provider's MFA when it can be checked. Add a per-provider setting, "accept this provider's MFA." When it's on and the ID token's amr claim shows a second factor, skip Cal.diy's 2FA. If amr is missing or shows only a password, require Cal.diy's 2FA. This can be in Sprint 4.
7. Fine, as long as accounts are matched by the provider's user ID (the sub claim), never by email. If the new email is already taken, keep the old one and tell the user.
8. A verified OIDC login with an invited email accepts the invite, even if "allow new accounts" is off for that provider.
9. Agreed, no group mapping for now.
10. Agreed.
11. Yes, 10 is enough.
12. Keycloak is fine. Document the setup so anyone on the team can run the tests.

import { ErrorCode } from "@calcom/lib/errorCodes";

export class ErrorWithCode extends Error {
  code: ErrorCode;
  data?: Record<string, unknown>;
  constructor(code: ErrorCode, message?: string, data?: Record<string, unknown>) {
    super(message);
    this.code = code;
    this.data = data;
  }
  static get Factory() {
    return new Proxy(ErrorWithCode, {
      get(_, prop: string) {
        if (prop in ErrorCode) {
          const code = ErrorCode[prop as keyof typeof ErrorCode];
          return (message?: string, data?: Record<string, unknown>) => new ErrorWithCode(code, message, data);
        }
        throw new Error(`Unknown error code: ${prop}`);
      },
    }) as unknown as Record<
      keyof typeof ErrorCode,
      (message?: string, data?: Record<string, unknown>) => ErrorWithCode
    >;
  }
}

/**
 * Converts unknown error types to Error objects.
 *
 * @deprecated For server-side code, use `getServerErrorFromUnknown` from `@calcom/lib/server/getServerErrorFromUnknown` instead.
 * This function should only be used in client-side or isomorphic code (React components, shared utilities).
 *
 * Use this function when:
 * - You're in a React component that runs on the client
 * - You're in shared/isomorphic code that cannot import server-only dependencies
 * - You only need a basic Error object without HTTP status code mapping
 *
 * For server-side error handling (API routes, tRPC handlers, webhooks), use `getServerErrorFromUnknown`
 * which provides proper HTTP status code mapping, error redaction, and handles Zod/Prisma/Stripe errors.
 *
 * @param cause - The unknown error to convert
 * @returns An Error object with optional statusCode and code properties
 */
export function getErrorFromUnknown(cause: unknown): Error & { statusCode?: number; code?: string } {
  if (cause instanceof Error) {
    return cause;
  }
  if (typeof cause === "string") {
    // @ts-ignore https://github.com/tc39/proposal-error-cause - must use @ts-ignore because different packages have different TS lib targets
    return new Error(cause, { cause });
  }

  return new Error(`Unhandled error of type '${typeof cause}''`);
}

  if (response.headers.get("content-encoding") === "gzip") {
    const responseText = await response.text();
    return new Promise((resolve) => resolve(JSON.parse(responseText)));

    response.json().then(console.log);
    throw Error(response.statusText);
  }

  return response.json();
}

Running late button for host
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

When a host is running late, their only option is to email the attendees personally that they are running late, which is not an ideal thing to do when you _are_ running late. 

### Describe the solution you would like

In the upcoming bookings, add a button that will notify attendees by email that the host is running late.

### User Story

As a host I want to be able to let attendees know when I am running late.

### User Scenario

A host is running late and hits a button that notifies attendees that the host is running late.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Hosts see a "Running late" action only on accepted bookings that start within the next 2 hours or are already in progress
- [ ] The host can pick a delay (5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes) and add an optional message before sending
- [ ] Every attendee gets an email with the event, the original start time in their timezone, the delay and the host's message
- [ ] Only the booking's host can send a notice, and sending it doesn't change the booking's time

### Out of Scope

- Sending non-email notifications (SMS, WhatsApp, etc)

### Open Questions

### Running late notice: open questions

- **Time window:** is "within the next 2 hours or in progress" the right range, or should it be configurable?
- **Team events:** can any host on the booking send the notice, or only the one assigned to it?
- **Repeat notices:** if a host sends a second notice, does it replace the first or add to it? Should there be a cap?
- **Notifying others:** should the host, or other hosts on the booking, get a copy of the email?
- **Guests:** does the notice go to guests added to the booking, or only the main attendees?
- **Delay presets:** are 5, 10, 15 and 30 minutes the right options?
- **Seated events:** should every seat holder get the email, or only some?
- **Calendar events:** should the notice update the event description in the host's or attendees' calendars?
- **Language:** should the email use each attendee's locale or the host's?
- **Record keeping:** should sent notices be logged, for example in the booking's audit log?

==== PR 81
### Summary

This PR adds the "Require reschedule reason" dropdown to Event Type, Advanced, next to the cancellation one. It passes the setting to the Request Reschedule dialog, which hides "(Optional)" and disables "Request reschedule" while a required reason is empty. It also changes the default from `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` to `OPTIONAL_BOTH`, in `schema.prisma`, in the existing migration and in `isRescheduleReasonRequired`.

The UI side looks right. The dialog uses the same `isRescheduleReasonRequired` helper as `requestReschedule.handler.ts:84`, so the button and the server agree. The repository select, the bookings query and the update schema all carry the new field. On `1d61ffc112`, lint, type checks and both unit test jobs pass in CI. The two red checks are not caused by this PR: `Check Prisma Migrations` fails because its workflow file is invalid (it fails the same way on #77), and `Security Audit` fails on third-party dependencies.

### Changes requested

#### 1. Do not edit a migration that is already on main

`20260916120000_add_reschedule_reason_require/migration.sql` merged with #36. A database that already ran it does not run it again, so this edit changes nothing there. The column keeps `DEFAULT 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY'`. Also, when that migration added the column, PostgreSQL filled every existing event type with `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`, not with NULL. So the new `?? OPTIONAL_BOTH` fallback never reaches those rows, and their hosts still must give a reason. That is the case this PR wants to prevent.

Please put the old migration back as it is on `main`, and add a new migration:

```sql
ALTER TABLE "EventType" ALTER COLUMN "requiresRescheduleReason" SET DEFAULT 'OPTIONAL_BOTH';
UPDATE "EventType" SET "requiresRescheduleReason" = 'OPTIONAL_BOTH' WHERE "requiresRescheduleReason" = 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY';
```

The `UPDATE` is safe now because nothing on `main` lets a host set this value, so every stored value came from the old default. After this PR merges, that is no longer true.

#### 2. Say why the default differs from #11

#11 asks for "the same four values and the same default posture" as the cancellation setting, and that default is `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`. `OPTIONAL_BOTH` is a reasonable choice, so existing event types do not change behavior. Please put that decision in the PR description with the alternative you did not take.

#### 3. Resolve the conflict and link the issue

The branch conflicts with `main` in `EventAdvancedTab.tsx`. The description also needs `Closes #11`, which the Sprint 1 spec asks for.

#### 4. Add tests and the test strategy

The only test change flips the expectation of one existing test. Please add tests for the new behavior: the dialog disables "Request reschedule" when a reason is required and the text is empty, enables it when there is text, and shows "(Optional)" only when no reason is required. A test that the Advanced tab saves the chosen value would also help. "How should this be tested?" still has the template prompts. Please replace them with the steps you used to check it.

### Minor

- The Checklist still has the template lines, for example the one that says the contributing guide was not read, and "My PR is too large". The template says to remove the lines that do not apply. As they are, they read as statements about this PR.
- `RescheduleDialog.tsx` moves the React imports, and `EventAdvancedTab.tsx` rewraps the cancellation `defaultValue`. If Biome made these changes, they are OK.

### Rubric

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness: does the change do what the issue asked? | 5 | The dropdown and the dialog work with the existing server check. The default change does not reach any database that already ran the #36 migration, and the branch conflicts with `main`. |
| Test coverage: are tests present and meaningful? | 4 | One existing test is updated for the new default. The dialog and the setting have no tests. |
| Code quality: consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | 7 | It follows the cancellation setting closely and reuses `isRescheduleReasonRequired`. Some formatting changes are unrelated. |
| Documentation: inline comments and PR description are clear | 4 | The description says what and why. The test section is the template, the checklist has template lines, and there is no `Closes #11`. |
| AI transparency: if AI was used, is there evidence of human verification? | 5 | Neither the PR nor #11 says whether AI was used. If it was, please link the log in a comment on #11. If not, one line there is enough. |
| Overall: would you merge this as-is? | 4 | Not as-is. After items 1, 3 and 4, yes. |
