 `./.claude/worktrees/agent-a72ec384ce096e641/specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md`

```text
1	# OIDC Sign-In Design
2	
3	Issue: #131. Sprints 3 and 4. Status: **draft, waiting for customer answers** (see `customer-questions.md`).
4	
5	Line numbers refer to `origin/main` at `e01d161c0c`.
6	
7	## Overview
8	
9	An instance admin connects Cal.diy to one or more OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity providers (Keycloak, Authentik, Okta, and others) from the admin settings page. Users then see "Continue with <provider>" on the login page and sign in with their organization account. Providers are stored in the database, so adding, editing or removing one needs no environment variable and no restart.
10	
11	## Problem Statement
12	
13	Self-hosted Cal.diy supports only email and password, Google and Microsoft login. Google and Microsoft are configured with environment variables at boot. Organizations that host Cal.diy already have their own identity provider, so their staff keep a second password for Cal.diy, and leaving the organization does not end Cal.diy access.
14	
15	## User Stories
16	
17	- As an instance admin, I want to connect our identity provider from the admin settings page, so that our staff log in with the account they already have.
18	- As a staff member, I want to click "Continue with University SSO" and come back logged in, so that I do not need a separate Cal.diy password.
19	- As an existing Cal.diy user, I want to link my organization login to my existing account, so that I keep my event types and bookings.
20	- As an instance admin, I want a broken or removed provider to fail safely, so that no one gets into an account that is not theirs and no one is locked out without a way back.
21	
22	## User Scenario
23	
24	An IT admin opens **Settings → Admin → Identity providers**, clicks **Add provider**, and enters the display name "University SSO", the issuer URL, the client ID and the client secret. The page shows the callback URL to register at the provider. The admin clicks **Test connection**; Cal.diy fetches the discovery document and shows "Connection OK". The admin saves and enables the provider.
25	
26	A professor opens the login page and clicks **Continue with University SSO**. The university login page opens. After sign-in, the professor returns to Cal.diy. The professor has no Cal.diy account yet, the provider says the email is verified, and new accounts are allowed for that provider, so Cal.diy creates the account and opens onboarding.
27	
28	A student whose email is not verified at the university tries the same button. Cal.diy rejects the login and shows "Your sign-in provider has not verified your email address. Verify it with your provider and try again."
29	
30	## Acceptance Criteria
31	
32	"Provider" below means an OIDC provider that an admin configured in Cal.diy. "Linked" means a Cal.diy user has an `Account` row for that provider's subject (`sub`).
33	
34	### Provider configuration (admin)
35	
36	1. An admin can add, edit, enable, disable and remove a provider at **Settings → Admin → Identity providers**. Each change takes effect on the next login request, with no environment change and no restart.
37	2. The page is visible only to users with role `ADMIN`. The role check is in `page.tsx`. Every tRPC procedure behind it uses `authedAdminProcedure`. A non-admin who calls a procedure directly gets `FORBIDDEN` and no data.
38	3. A provider has: display name (1–50 characters), issuer URL, client ID, client secret, scopes (default `openid email profile`), "allow new accounts" (default off), "allowed email domains" (optional list), and enabled (default off). Each field is validated, and an invalid field shows a message next to it. Save is blocked until every field is valid.
39	4. The issuer URL must be `https`. `http` is accepted only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or a `*.localhost` host, so that a local test provider works. Scopes must include `openid`.
40	5. **Test connection** fetches `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration` from the server with a 5-second timeout. It reports one of: OK; unreachable (network error or timeout); not a discovery document (bad JSON or missing `authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint` or `jwks_uri`); issuer mismatch (the document's `issuer` is not the configured issuer); `authorization_code` grant or `code` response type not supported. Saving does not require a passing test, but enabling a provider does.
41	6. The client secret is encrypted at rest with `symmetricEncrypt` and `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. No API response, log line, page source or error message contains the secret, encrypted or plain. The edit form shows "Secret is set" and a "Replace secret" field; leaving it empty keeps the stored secret.
42	7. The page shows the callback URL (`<WEBAPP_URL>/api/auth/callback/<provider id>`) with a copy button, before and after the first save.
43	8. Two admins who edit the same provider at the same time: the later save wins, and the page shows the saved values after reload. (No merge.)
44	9. At most 10 providers can exist. Adding an eleventh shows a message and saves nothing.
45	10. If `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing or not 32 bytes, the page shows an error that names the variable, and add or edit of a secret is blocked. Existing password, Google and Microsoft login keep working.
46	
47	### Login and sign-up
48	
49	11. The login page shows one "Continue with <display name>" button for each enabled provider, in the order the admin set, below the Google and Microsoft buttons. The button text uses the translated template `continue_with_provider`; only the display name comes from the admin. With no enabled provider, the login page looks exactly as it does today.
50	12. The sign-up page shows the same buttons only for providers with "allow new accounts" on.
51	13. Clicking a button starts an authorization code flow with PKCE and `state` checks. User data comes from the ID token claims (`idToken: true`).
52	14. A first login with a verified email, no existing Cal.diy user with that email, "allow new accounts" on, and the email domain on the allowed list (or no list): Cal.diy creates a user with `identityProvider = OIDC`, `identityProviderId = null`, `emailVerified` set, the name from the `name` claim, and an `Account` row for (provider id, `sub`). The user and the `Account` row are created in one transaction, so a failed link leaves no orphan user that owns the email. The user lands in onboarding.
53	15. A login where `email_verified` is missing or `false` is rejected with `/auth/error?error=unverified-email` and the existing message `unverified_email_oauth_error`. No user and no `Account` row is created or changed.
54	16. A login with no `email` claim is rejected with a new error `missing-email` and a message that tells the user to ask their admin to release the email claim. Nothing is created.
55	17. A login with no `name` claim does not fail. The name falls back to `preferred_username`, then to the part of the email before `@`. (Today `signIn` returns `false` for a missing name, at `next-auth-options.ts:847`.)
56	18. A first login when "allow new accounts" is off, or the email domain is not on the allowed list, is rejected with a new error `oidc-signup-not-allowed`. The message says the account does not exist and names no reason that would reveal the domain list.
57	19. A returning linked user signs in as the user that owns the `Account` row, found by (provider id, `sub`), never by email. This holds after the user's email changes at the provider.
58	20. A linked user with Cal.diy 2FA enabled still gets the TOTP step (`loginWithTotp`), as Google users do today.
59	21. A user who sends a forged or expired `state`, or replays a callback, gets the login page with a "sign-in failed, try again" message, and no session.
60	
61	### Failures at the provider
62	
63	22. Provider down, slow (no answer in 5 seconds) or discovery URL unreachable when the user clicks the button: the user returns to the login page with the message "We could not reach <display name>. Try again later or use another sign-in method." Today next-auth sends `?error=OAuthSignin` to `/auth/login`, and `login-view.tsx` does not read `error` from the URL, so the user sees nothing. The login page must read and show `OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback` and `AccessDenied`.
64	23. Wrong client secret or wrong client ID: the token exchange fails, and the user sees "Sign-in with <display name> is not set up correctly. Contact your administrator." The server logs the provider id and the error code, not the secret.
65	24. A provider that is disabled or removed while a user is on its login page: the callback is rejected with the message from criterion 23. No user is created.
66	25. A request to `/api/auth/signin/<id>` for a disabled or unknown provider id does not start a flow and shows the generic sign-in error.
67	26. One broken provider does not affect the others or password login. Loading the provider list from the database must not throw; a provider whose secret fails to decrypt is skipped and logged.
68	
69	### Existing accounts and conflicts
70	
71	27. A first OIDC login whose verified email matches an existing Cal.diy user who has no link to this provider follows the account-linking rule in ADR-004. **Until the customer answers Q1, the rule is "reject": the user sees `oidc-account-exists` ("An account with this email already exists. Sign in with your usual method, then link <display name> in Settings → Security.")**, and nothing changes on the existing account. This message confirms that an account exists for that email. We accept that, because the user has just proved control of that email at the provider; criterion 18 still hides the domain list.
72	28. OIDC logins never reach the existing shared paths: the `identityProvider + identityProviderId` lookups in `signIn` (`next-auth-options.ts:891–911`, the legacy fix at L914–932) and in `jwt` (L601–612); the "verified and not CAL" branch at L1012; the "CAL user with verified email" re-link at L1051; and the email-based `autoMergeIdentities()` fallback in `jwt` (L594, L615). For `oidc-*` providers the only identity lookup is the `Account` row (provider, `sub`), and `jwt` takes the user id from the `user` that next-auth resolved, never from `token.email`. The adapter's legacy fallback in `next-auth-custom-adapter.ts:90–104` stays limited to Google and SAML. A test proves each path is not reached.
73	29. An email match with an invited user (no password, not verified, no username; the branch at L1021) is treated as an existing account, not as a free claim, unless the customer says otherwise (Q1).
74	30. Two providers assert the same email: the user is linked to provider A, and provider B sends the same verified email with a different `sub`. Provider B's login is handled as criterion 27. Provider B never signs the user in through provider A's link. The reverse case is also tested: provider B sends the same `sub` that the user has at provider A; B's login is a new identity and never matches the user.
75	31. A returning linked user whose email changed at the provider: Cal.diy updates the user's email only if the new email is verified, is not used by another user (compared case-insensitively), and passes the provider's allowed domains. The new email and `email_verified` are read from the raw ID-token claims (`profile`), not from next-auth's `user` object, which holds the stored user once an `Account` row exists. If another user has the new email, the login is rejected with `new-email-conflict` (existing message) and nothing changes.
76	32. Organization auto-join (`ORGANIZATIONS_AUTOLINK`, L130) does not apply to OIDC users in this feature.
77	
78	### User account settings
79	
80	33. **Settings → Security** lists the providers the user is linked to, with the date each was linked.
81	34. A signed-in user can link an enabled provider from that page. Linking starts the same flow and adds an `Account` row to the signed-in user, even if the provider's email differs from the Cal.diy email. It fails with a message if that (provider, `sub`) is already linked to another user. The reject rule in criterion 27 does not block this flow: `signIn` knows the signed-in user's id and allows the link when the email match is that same user. The link flow sends `prompt=login`, so a browser already signed in at the provider as someone else cannot attach that identity silently, and the page shows the provider's email before it confirms.
82	35. A user can unlink a provider only if another login method remains: a password, another linked provider, Google or Microsoft. Otherwise the unlink button is disabled, and the page explains how to set a password first (the existing `createAccountPassword` flow).
83	
84	### Provider removal and old data
85	
86	36. Removing a provider that has linked users requires the admin to type the provider's display name. The confirmation shows how many users are linked and how many of them have no other login method.
87	37. Removing a provider deletes its `Account` rows. Users whose only login was that provider keep their account and data. They can recover with "Forgot password", because `createAccountPassword` already serves non-`CAL` users. (To confirm in implementation: the forgot-password email reaches `OIDC` users.)
88	38. Disabling a provider hides its button and blocks its logins, and keeps its links, so enabling it again restores access.
89	39. Upgrading an instance that has users and no providers: the migration adds an empty provider table and one enum value. Login, sign-up, sessions, Google, Microsoft and password login behave exactly as before. No existing row changes.
90	40. Downgrading after providers exist is not supported. The migration notes say so.
91	
92	### Password login and lock-out (Sprint 4, waits on Q4)
93	
94	41. If the customer wants a "disable password login" switch: it can be turned on only while at least one provider is enabled and the admin who turns it on is linked to an enabled provider. Users with role `ADMIN` can always log in with a password, so an admin cannot lock every admin out.
95	
96	### Test setup
97	
98	42. A Keycloak instance runs locally from a separate compose file with a realm export that has three test users: verified email, unverified email, and no email claim. The README gives the steps from a clean clone to a working login in under 15 minutes.
99	43. Unit tests cover the provider service (validation, encryption, discovery test results), the identity-provider mapping, and each `signIn` branch above. An end-to-end test against Keycloak covers criteria 14 and 15.
100	
101	## Proposed answers to the open questions in #131
102	
103	Each answer is a proposal. **Every one needs customer confirmation**; the questions are in `customer-questions.md`.
104	
105	| #131 question | Proposed answer | Criteria |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| Same email already exists; how to prevent takeover? | Do not auto-link by email by default. Reject and require linking from settings, or auto-link only for domains the admin marks as owned by that provider. Never auto-link to an `ADMIN` account. Needs customer confirmation. | 27–30 |
108	| Who may create an account through OIDC? | Per provider: "allow new accounts" (default off) plus an optional allowed-domains list. Needs customer confirmation, including whether `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_SIGNUP` also blocks OIDC sign-up. | 12, 14, 18 |
109	| What does the user see if the provider is down or misconfigured? | A message that names the provider and offers other sign-in methods; admins get a test button. Needs customer confirmation of wording only. | 5, 22–26 |
110	| More than one provider? Turn off password login? | Yes, up to 10. Password-login switch only in Sprint 4, with an admin break-glass rule. Needs customer confirmation. | 9, 41 |
111	| How are secrets stored, who can see them? | Encrypted with the instance key; write-only in the UI; only `ADMIN` can change them; no one can read them back. Needs customer confirmation. | 6 |
112	| Unlink? Only login method? | Yes, unless it is the last login method. Needs customer confirmation. | 35 |
113	| Groups to roles? | No in Sprints 3–4. Record in future work. Needs customer confirmation. | none |
114	| How to test without a real IdP? | Local Keycloak with a realm export. Needs customer confirmation that Keycloak is acceptable as the reference provider. | 42–43 |
115	| Existing data after upgrade? | No behavior change until an admin adds a provider. Needs customer confirmation. | 39–40 |
116	
117	## Open questions not listed in #131
118	
119	These came from reading the code. They are also in `customer-questions.md`.
120	
121	- Does the site-wide "require 2FA" rule (#112, PR #120) apply to OIDC users? Today `requiresTwoFactorSetup` exempts every non-`CAL` user, so OIDC users would be exempt. Proposed: exempt, because the provider owns MFA.
122	- Some providers do not send `email_verified`. Should an admin be able to mark a provider as "emails are always verified"? Proposed: no, because that is the takeover path.
123	- Should a returning user's email follow the provider when it changes? Proposed: yes, with the checks in criterion 31.
124	- Is an invited user (L1021) a free claim for anyone whose provider asserts that email? Proposed: no.
125	- Should OIDC users be put into an organization by email domain? Proposed: no in this feature.
126	- What does the user see after removal of their only login method? Proposed: criterion 37.
127	
128	## Technical Design
129	
130	### Database Changes (needs a yes before any edit to `schema.prisma`)
131	
132	- Add `OIDC` to `enum IdentityProvider` (`schema.prisma:367`).
133	- Add model `OidcProvider`: `id` (cuid, immutable, used in the NextAuth provider id `oidc-<id>`), `displayName`, `issuer`, `clientId`, `clientSecretEncrypted`, `scopes`, `allowSignup` (default false), `allowedDomains` (String[]), `enabled` (default false), `position` (Int), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `updatedById`.
134	- No change to `User` or `Account`. The link is an `Account` row with `provider = "oidc-<id>"` and `providerAccountId = sub`. `@@unique([provider, providerAccountId])` (L1258) already makes one `sub` belong to one user per provider. See ADR-002.
135	
136	### Server
137	
138	- `PrismaOidcProviderRepository` (data access only) and `OidcProviderService` (validation, encryption, discovery test), wired with the moduleLoader DI pattern in `packages/features/auth/oidc/di/`.
139	- `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts` becomes an async handler that loads enabled providers and passes them to `getOptions`. `getOptions` gains a `dynamicProviders` argument and stays synchronous. See ADR-001.
140	- Each provider becomes a NextAuth `type: "oauth"` provider with `wellKnown`, `idToken: true`, `checks: ["pkce", "state"]`, and **no** `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking`. `httpOptions.timeout` is set to 5000 ms (to confirm the option name for next-auth 4.24.13).
141	- `getIdentityProvider` maps any id that starts with `oidc-` to `IdentityProvider.OIDC`. `signIn` gets a separate OIDC branch before the shared code, so OIDC never reaches the auto-merge branches (criterion 28). The `jwt` callback resolves OIDC users through the `Account` row, not through `token.email`.
142	- New-user and link paths call `calcomAdapter.linkAccount` inside `signIn`, in the same transaction as any user write, so that next-auth's own callback handler finds the account by (provider, `sub`) and does not need email linking. Confirmed in the next-auth 4.24.13 source by the Deep review: `routes/callback` calls `getUserByAccount`, then the `signIn` callback, then `callbackHandler`, which looks up the account again before any email match. In `signIn`, `user` is the stored user when an `Account` row exists, otherwise the `profile()` output; `profile` holds the raw ID-token claims.
143	- `signIn` receives no session. `getOptions` gains a `getSessionUserId` getter (like `getDubId`), so the OIDC branch can tell a settings link (criterion 34) from a login.
144	- Admin tRPC procedures under `viewer.admin`: `oidcProviders.list`, `create`, `update`, `setEnabled`, `delete`, `testDiscovery`. All use `authedAdminProcedure`. List returns a DTO without the secret.
145	- Public read for the login and sign-up pages: id and display name of enabled providers only, read in `getServerSideProps`.
146	
147	### UI
148	
149	- Admin: new page `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/settings/(admin-layout)/admin/identity-providers/page.tsx` (role check here), view in `apps/web/modules/settings/admin/identity-providers-view.tsx`. Follows `security/page.tsx`.
150	- Login: buttons in `apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.tsx` after the Microsoft button (~L215), using `signIn("oidc-<id>")` and `useLastUsed`. Read `error` from the URL and show it.
151	- Error page: add messages for `missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists`, `unknown-provider` in `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx`.
152	- Settings → Security: "Connected logins" section (Sprint 4).
153	- Every string goes in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`. The existing `sso_oidc_*` strings belong to the removed team SSO feature; reuse `sso_oidc_callback_copied` only.
154	
155	## Edge Cases
156	
157	Covered by the criteria above. The short list:
158	
159	- Provider down, slow, unreachable discovery, bad secret, issuer mismatch: 5, 22–26.
160	- Unverified, missing email, missing name: 15–17.
161	- Email matches an existing account, invited user, two providers with one email: 27–30.
162	- Email change at the provider: 31.
163	- Provider disabled or removed with dependent users; only-login users: 24, 36–38.
164	- Admin lock-out: 41.
165	- Upgrade with old data: 39–40.
166	- Missing encryption key: 10.
167	- Concurrent admin edits: 8.
168	
169	## Out of Scope
170	
171	- SAML changes (#131).
172	- Single logout at the provider (#131).
173	- Changes to Google or Microsoft login, including their `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking: true`.
174	- Mapping provider groups or claims to Cal.diy roles or teams.
175	- Organization or team-level SSO (the old Jackson-based feature).
176	- Per-provider button icons or colors.
177	- API v2 endpoints for provider management.

```text
1	# OIDC Sign-In Decisions
2	
3	Status of each ADR: **Proposed** (team picks, spec review confirms), **Customer** (the customer decides; we propose), or **Owner** (Zachary or the team decides before the PR that needs it).
4	
5	## ADR-001: How providers reach NextAuth without a restart
6	
7	Status: Proposed.
8	
9	### Context
10	
11	Today `providers` is a module-level array built once at import (`next-auth-options.ts:307–370`), and `getOptions` is synchronous. Criterion 1 requires a change to take effect on the next login with no restart. `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts` already calls `NextAuth(req, res, getOptions(...))` on every request, so options can differ per request.
12	
13	### Options Considered
14	
15	1. **Load enabled providers from the database on each `/api/auth/*` request.** The handler awaits a repository call, then passes the result to `getOptions`. Pros: always current, no invalidation logic, correct on several server instances. Cons: one indexed query per auth request (sign-in, callback, session, CSRF). Auth traffic is small next to booking traffic, and the table holds at most 10 rows.
16	2. **Cache providers in memory with invalidation on admin save.** Pros: no query on most requests. Cons: each server instance has its own cache, so a save on instance A is stale on instance B until a TTL expires; this breaks criterion 1 on any multi-instance deploy unless we add Redis pub/sub. More code to review.
17	3. **Build providers at boot from the database.** Pros: no change to `getOptions`. Cons: needs a restart, which fails criterion 1.
18	
19	### Decision
20	
21	Option 1. `getOptions` gains a `dynamicProviders: Provider[]` argument and stays synchronous, so its other callers do not change. Only the NextAuth route handler awaits the load. If a profile shows the query matters, add option 2 behind the same repository method later (recorded in `future-work.md`).
22	
23	### Consequences
24	
25	- Every caller of `getOptions` must be checked. Callers that do not handle sign-in (for example session decoding) pass an empty list.
26	- A database outage also breaks OIDC sign-in. Password login already needs the database, so this adds no new failure mode.
27	
28	## ADR-002: How a user's OIDC link is stored
29	
30	Status: Proposed. Needs a yes before any edit to `schema.prisma`.
31	
32	### Context
33	
34	`User.identityProvider` is one enum (`CAL | GOOGLE | SAML | AZUREAD`) and `User.identityProviderId` is one string. Admins create providers at run time, and two providers can issue the same `sub`. `getIdentityProvider` returns `null` for unknown ids, which sends `signIn` to `unknown-provider` and `jwt` to the email-based auto-merge.
35	
36	### Options Considered
37	
38	1. **One `OIDC` enum value; the link is an `Account` row with `provider = "oidc-<id>"`, `providerAccountId = sub`.** Pros: `Account` already has `@@unique([provider, providerAccountId])`, so one `sub` per provider maps to one user; a user can hold links to several providers; no `User` column change. Cons: OIDC lookups must use `Account`, not `User.identityProviderId`, so the OIDC path cannot share the existing lookup at L891.
39	2. **One `OIDC` enum value plus a new `User.identityProviderConfigId` column.** Pros: keeps the existing `identityProvider + identityProviderId` lookup. Cons: one link per user only, so linking a second provider overwrites the first; a second migration on the largest table.
40	3. **One enum value per provider.** Cons: enums are fixed at migration time, so an admin cannot add one at run time. Rejected outright.
41	
42	### Decision
43	
44	Option 1. New OIDC users get `identityProvider = OIDC` and `identityProviderId = null`. Storing `sub` there would be unsafe: the shared lookups at L891, L914 and L601 match on `identityProvider + identityProviderId` with no provider id, so provider B asserting the `sub` a user has at provider A would match that user (found by the Deep review). Existing users who link a provider keep their `identityProvider`, so their password or Google login keeps working.
45	
46	### Consequences
47	
48	- `getIdentityProvider` maps the `oidc-` prefix to `OIDC`.
49	- Removing a provider means deleting its `Account` rows (criterion 37).
50	- `requiresTwoFactorSetup` treats `OIDC` as non-`CAL`, so OIDC users are exempt from site-wide 2FA unless the customer says otherwise (Q6).
51	
52	## ADR-003: Provider id in URLs and `Account.provider`
53	
54	Status: Proposed.
55	
56	### Options Considered
57	
58	1. **Immutable database id (`oidc-<cuid>`).** Pros: renaming the display name never breaks links or the registered callback URL. Cons: the callback URL is not human-readable.
59	2. **Admin-chosen slug (`oidc-university`).** Pros: readable URL. Cons: editing the slug breaks every link and the URL registered at the provider, so the slug would have to be locked after creation, which is option 1 with extra rules.
60	
61	### Decision
62	
63	Option 1.
64	
65	## ADR-004: What happens when an OIDC email matches an existing account
66	
67	Status: **Customer** (Q1). We propose; we do not pick. This path gets a narrow Deep (Fable 5.1) review before implementation.
68	
69	### Context
70	
71	Any provider an admin adds can assert any email, including the email of the instance admin. Google and Microsoft use `allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking: true` and the `signIn` branches at L1012 and L1051 merge on a verified email. If OIDC used the same paths, a misconfigured or hostile provider, or a user who can set their own email at a self-service provider, could take over any account. The `jwt` callback's `autoMergeIdentities()` (L453) also finds the user by `token.email`, so a wrong `true` from `signIn` becomes a session for the email's owner.
72	
73	### Options Considered
74	
75	1. **Auto-link on verified email.** Pros: no friction; matches Google and Microsoft today. Cons: account takeover whenever a provider asserts an email it does not own. Self-service providers (Keycloak with user registration on, or a provider that lets users edit their email) make this easy.
76	2. **Reject and require linking from settings.** The user signs in with their existing method, then clicks "Link" in Settings → Security, which proves control of both accounts. Pros: no takeover path; simple to test. Cons: one extra step for every existing user at roll-out.
77	3. **Auto-link only for allowed domains.** Each provider has a list of email domains the admin says the provider owns. A verified email in that list auto-links; any other match is rejected as in option 2. Accounts with role `ADMIN` never auto-link. Pros: smooth roll-out for the organization's own domain; takeover risk limited to domains the admin vouched for. Cons: more rules to test; a wrong list is still a takeover path for that domain.
78	
79	### Proposal to the customer
80	
81	Option 3 with option 2 as the fallback, and no auto-link for `ADMIN` accounts. Sprint 3 ships option 2 only (reject), because it is safe under every answer and the Sprint 3 demo needs only new accounts.
82	
83	### Consequences
84	
85	- The OIDC branch must never fall through to L1012, L1021, L1051 or `autoMergeIdentities()`. A test per branch (criterion 28).
86	- Linking from settings (sub-issue 6) is needed for existing users under options 2 and 3.
87	
88	## ADR-005: Where the OIDC logic sits in `signIn` and `jwt`
89	
90	Status: Proposed.
91	
92	### Options Considered
93	
94	1. **A separate OIDC branch at the top of `signIn`, in its own service (`OidcSignInService`), returning before the shared code.** Pros: the shared Google/Azure/SAML branches stay untouched (Google and Microsoft are out of scope); the OIDC rules are testable without the 400-line callback; follows the factory rule (conditionals at the entry point). Cons: some duplication of user-creation code.
95	2. **Add `OIDC` cases to the existing branches.** Pros: less new code. Cons: every existing branch gains an OIDC condition; a missed condition is a takeover (ADR-004); review must re-read all of `signIn`.
96	
97	### Decision
98	
99	Option 1. `signIn` checks `account.provider.startsWith("oidc-")` once and delegates. The `jwt` callback does the same and takes the user id from the `user` that next-auth resolved through the `Account` row.
100	
101	### Rules from the Deep review (2026-11-09)
102	
103	A narrow Fable 5.1 review of the `signIn`, `jwt` and adapter paths found these rules necessary. Each needs a test in sub-issue 5 or 7.
104	
105	1. For `oidc-*` the only identity lookup is `Account(provider, providerAccountId)`. Never query `identityProviderId` for OIDC (cross-provider `sub` collision).
106	2. Never add OIDC to the adapter's legacy `identityProviderId` fallback (`next-auth-custom-adapter.ts:90–104`).
107	3. `signIn` knows the session user (via a `getSessionUserId` getter in `getOptions`), so a settings link to the user's own email is not rejected by the Sprint 3 rule, and a link to another user's email is.
108	4. Create the user and the `Account` row in one transaction. Otherwise a failed `linkAccount` leaves a user who owns the email, and next-auth's email check then blocks that person.
109	5. The link flow uses `prompt=login` and shows the provider's email before confirming (lower risk; prevents attaching an identity from a stale provider session).
110	
111	## ADR-006: How the client secret is stored
112	
113	Status: Proposed.
114	
115	### Options Considered
116	
117	1. **Encrypt with `symmetricEncrypt` and `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in the provider row.** Pros: existing precedent (`packages/lib/crypto.ts`); no new dependency; works with criterion 1. Cons: anyone with the database and the key can read secrets; AES-256-CBC without authentication (same as existing credentials).
118	2. **Store the name of an environment variable that holds the secret.** Pros: secret never in the database. Cons: needs an environment change and restart for each new provider, which fails criterion 1.
119	3. **Store plain text.** Cons: a database dump leaks every secret. Rejected.
120	
121	(Hashing is not possible: the server must send the secret to the provider.)
122	
123	### Decision
124	
125	Option 1. The secret is write-only in the UI and absent from every DTO.
126	
127	## ADR-007: User data from the ID token or the userinfo endpoint
128	
129	Status: Proposed.
130	
131	### Options Considered
132	
133	1. **ID token claims (`idToken: true`).** Pros: signed by the provider and checked against its JWKS; one fewer request. Cons: some providers put `email` only in userinfo unless configured.
134	2. **Userinfo endpoint.** Pros: always has the profile claims. Cons: extra request that can fail; data not signed.
135	
136	### Decision
137	
138	Option 1. If the ID token has no `email`, the login fails with `missing-email` (criterion 16), and the admin docs say how to release the claim in Keycloak, Authentik and Okta.
139	
140	## ADR-008: Test identity provider
141	
142	Status: **Owner** (where the compose service lives).
143	
144	### Options Considered
145	
146	1. **Keycloak in a separate compose file under `specs/oidc-sign-in/test-idp/` (or `docker/`), with a realm export.** Pros: real provider; teammates who do not work on OIDC run nothing new; no change to the shared `docker-compose.yml`. Cons: one more command to start.
147	2. **Add Keycloak to `docker-compose.yml`.** Pros: one command. Cons: every teammate pulls and runs a ~500 MB image; changes a shared file.
148	3. **A small mock OIDC server (for example `oidc-provider` in Node) for unit and CI tests.** Pros: fast, scriptable claims. Cons: not a real provider; a new dev dependency (needs a yes).
149	
150	### Proposal
151	
152	Option 1 for manual and end-to-end tests; unit tests mock the provider response and need no server. Option 3 only if CI needs it later.
153	
154	## ADR-009: Removing a provider that users depend on
155	
156	Status: Proposed.
157	
158	### Options Considered
159	
160	1. **Allow delete with a typed confirmation that shows linked and only-login user counts; delete the `Account` rows; users recover by password reset.** Pros: admin stays in control; nobody loses data. Cons: some users must reset a password.
161	2. **Block delete while any user is linked; offer disable only.** Pros: no one loses a login. Cons: an admin who changed providers can never clean up.
162	3. **Delete with no warning.** Cons: silent lock-out. Rejected.
163	
164	### Decision
165	
166	Option 1, plus disable (criterion 38) as the reversible choice the page offers first.

45	### 1. OIDC provider data model and repository (M, Sprint 3)
46	
47	Add `OIDC` to `enum IdentityProvider` and a new `OidcProvider` model (fields in design.md, Database Changes) with a migration. Add `PrismaOidcProviderRepository` (`findEnabled`, `findById`, `list`, `create`, `update`, `delete`, `countLinkedUsers`) using `select`, never `include`, and wire it with the moduleLoader DI pattern. The secret column stores only ciphertext. Criteria 3 (shape), 9, 39, 40. Unit tests for the repository with a mocked Prisma client. **Needs a yes before editing `schema.prisma`** (project rule). ~250 lines. Verifiable without the dev server.

50	
51	Add a compose file and a realm export with one client (`cal-diy`, confidential, redirect URI `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/*`) and three users: verified email, unverified email, no email claim. Add a README with exact start and stop commands and the values to paste into the admin page. Where the compose service lives is an owner's call (ADR-008). Criterion 42. ~150 lines, mostly JSON.

54	
55	Add `OidcProviderService`: field validation (criteria 3, 4), secret encryption with `symmetricEncrypt` and a clear error when `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is bad (6, 10), and `testDiscovery` with a 5-second timeout that returns one of the results in criterion 5. Add `viewer.admin.oidcProviders.{list,create,update,setEnabled,delete,testDiscovery}` on `authedAdminProcedure`; `list` returns a DTO with no secret field (2, 6). Enabling requires a passing discovery test. Unit tests cover each validation error, each discovery result and the non-admin `FORBIDDEN` path. ~400 lines with tests. Verifiable without the dev server.
56

58	
59	Add `settings/(admin-layout)/admin/identity-providers/page.tsx` with the `ADMIN` role check in the page, and a view in `apps/web/modules/settings/admin/`. List providers; add and edit form with inline errors; write-only secret field ("Secret is set" / "Replace secret"); callback URL with copy button; Test connection button with its result; enable and disable switch; reorder. Every string in `common.json`. Criteria 1–9. Delete with typed confirmation moves to row 9. ~400 lines. Needs a browser.
60

62	
63	Make the NextAuth route handler async: load enabled providers through the repository and pass them to `getOptions` as `dynamicProviders` (ADR-001). Build each as a next-auth `oauth` provider with `wellKnown`, `idToken: true`, PKCE and state, a 5-second HTTP timeout, and no dangerous email linking. Map the `oidc-` prefix to `IdentityProvider.OIDC`. Add `OidcSignInService`, called from the top of `signIn` and `jwt` (ADR-005): reject unverified (15), missing email (16), name fallback (17), sign-up rules (18), create the user and `Account` row (14), find returning users by (provider, `sub`) (19), keep TOTP (20), and reject any email match with `oidc-account-exists` (27, Sprint 3 rule). Create the user and `Account` row in one transaction; leave `identityProviderId` null. A test per branch, including criterion 28 (no path reaches the shared lookups or auto-merge code) and a two-providers-one-`sub` test (criterion 30). Rules 1–4 from the Deep review in ADR-005 apply. ~450 lines with tests. **Gets a narrow Deep review of the `signIn` and `jwt` changes before merge.** Verifiable with unit tests; the demo needs row 2.

Add the new error codes to `/auth/error` (`missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists`, `unknown-provider`). ~200 lines. Needs a browser.

254	@@ -0,0 +1,127 @@
255	+import {
256	+  RUNNING_LATE_DELAY_OPTIONS,
257	+  RUNNING_LATE_MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH,
258	+  type RunningLateDelayMinutes,
259	+} from "@calcom/features/bookings/lib/runningLate";
260	+import { Dialog } from "@calcom/features/components/controlled-dialog";
261	+import { useLocale } from "@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale";
262	+import { trpc } from "@calcom/trpc/react";
263	+import { Button } from "@calcom/ui/components/button";
264	+import { DialogContent, DialogFooter, DialogHeader } from "@calcom/ui/components/dialog";
265	+import { Label, Select, TextArea } from "@calcom/ui/components/form";
266	+import { showToast } from "@calcom/ui/components/toast";
267	+import type { Dispatch, SetStateAction } from "react";
268	+import { Controller, useForm } from "react-hook-form";
269	+
270	+interface IRunningLateDialog {
271	+  isOpenDialog: boolean;
272	+  setIsOpenDialog: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>;
273	+  bookingId: number;
274	+}
275	+
276	+interface FormValues {
277	+  delayMinutes: RunningLateDelayMinutes;
278	+  message: string;
279	+}
280	+
281	+export const RunningLateDialog = ({ isOpenDialog, setIsOpenDialog, bookingId }: IRunningLateDialog) => {
282	+  const { t } = useLocale();
283	+
284	+  const { control, handleSubmit, reset } = useForm<FormValues>({
285	+    defaultValues: {
286	+      delayMinutes: RUNNING_LATE_DELAY_OPTIONS[0],
287	+      message: "",
288	+    },
289	+  });
290	+
291	+  const { mutate: sendRunningLate, isPending } = trpc.viewer.bookings.runningLate.useMutation({
292	+    onSuccess(data) {
293	+      if (data.sent === 0) {
294	+        showToast(t("running_late_no_recipients"), "warning");
295	+      } else {
296	+        showToast(t("running_late_sent_toast", { count: data.sent }), "success");
297	+      }
298	+      reset();
299	+      setIsOpenDialog(false);
300	+    },
301	+    onError(error) {
302	+      showToast(error.message || t("unexpected_error_try_again"), "error");
303	+    },
304	+  });
305	+
306	+  const onSubmit = (data: FormValues) => {
307	+    sendRunningLate({
308	+      bookingId,
309	+      delayMinutes: data.delayMinutes,
310	+      message: data.message.trim() || undefined,
311	+    });
312	+  };
313	+
314	+  const delayOptions = RUNNING_LATE_DELAY_OPTIONS.map((minutes) => ({
315	+    label: t("running_late_delay_minutes", { count: minutes }),
316	+    value: minutes,
317	+  }));
318	+
319	+  return (
320	+    <Dialog open={isOpenDialog} onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}>
321	+      <DialogContent enableOverflow>
322	+        <form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}>
323	+          <DialogHeader title={t("running_late")} subtitle={t("running_late_dialog_description")} />
324	+          <div className="mb-4">
325	+            <Label htmlFor="delayMinutes" className="mb-2 block font-medium text-emphasis text-sm">
326	+              {t("running_late_delay_label")}
327	+            </Label>
328	+            <Controller
329	+              name="delayMinutes"
330	+              control={control}
331	+              render={({ field }) => (
332	+                <Select
333	+                  {...field}
334	+                  inputId="delayMinutes"
335	+                  options={delayOptions}
336	+                  onChange={(option) => {
337	+                    if (option) field.onChange(option.value);
338	+                  }}
339	+                  value={delayOptions.find((opt) => opt.value === field.value)}
340	+                />
341	+              )}
342	+            />
343	+          </div>
344	+
345	+          <div className="mb-4">
346	+            <Label htmlFor="message" className="mb-2 block font-medium text-emphasis text-sm">
347	+              {t("running_late_message_label")}{" "}
348	+              <span className="font-normal text-subtle">({t("optional")})</span>
349	+            </Label>
350	+            <Controller
351	+              name="message"
352	+              control={control}
353	+              render={({ field }) => (
354	+                <TextArea
355	+                  {...field}
356	+                  id="message"
357	+                  maxLength={RUNNING_LATE_MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH}
358	+                  placeholder={t("running_late_message_placeholder")}
359	+                  rows={3}
360	+                />
361	+              )}
362	+            />
363	+          </div>
364	+
365	+          <DialogFooter showDivider className="mt-8">
366	+            <Button
367	+              type="button"
368	+              color="secondary"
369	+              onClick={() => setIsOpenDialog(false)}
370	+              disabled={isPending}>
371	+              {t("cancel")}
372	+            </Button>
373	+            <Button type="submit" color="primary" disabled={isPending} loading={isPending}>
374	+              {t("running_late_send")}
375	+            </Button>
376	+          </DialogFooter>
377	+        </form>
378	+      </DialogContent>
379	+    </Dialog>
380	+  );
381	+};

432	@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
433	+import type { TFunction } from "i18next";
434	+import renderEmail from "../src/renderEmail";
435	+import BaseEmail from "./_base-email";
436	+
437	+export type AttendeeRunningLateEmailData = {
438	+  attendee: {
439	+    name: string;
440	+    email: string;
441	+    timeZone: string;
442	+    locale: string;
443	+  };
444	+  hostName: string;
445	+  hostEmail: string;
446	+  eventTitle: string;
447	+  startTime: Date;
448	+  delayMinutes: number;
449	+  message?: string;
450	+  t: TFunction;
451	+};
452	+
453	+export default class AttendeeRunningLateEmail extends BaseEmail {
454	+  constructor(private data: AttendeeRunningLateEmailData) {
455	+    super();
456	+    this.name = "SEND_RUNNING_LATE_EMAIL";
457	+  }
458	+
459	+  protected getTimezone(): string {
460	+    return this.data.attendee.timeZone;
461	+  }
462	+
463	+  protected getLocale(): string {
464	+    return this.data.attendee.locale;
465	+  }
466	+
467	+  protected async getNodeMailerPayload(): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
468	+    const { t, attendee, hostName, hostEmail, eventTitle, delayMinutes, message } = this.data;
469	+    const originalStart = `${this.getFormattedRecipientTime({
470	+      time: this.data.startTime.toISOString(),
471	+      format: "dddd, LL LT",
472	+    })} (${attendee.timeZone})`;
473	+    const delay = t("running_late_delay_minutes", { count: delayMinutes });
474	+
475	+    const textLines = [
476	+      t("running_late_email_title", { hostName, interpolation: { escapeValue: false } }),
477	+      `${t("what")}: ${eventTitle}`,
478	+      `${t("running_late_original_start")}: ${originalStart}`,
479	+      `${t("running_late_expected_delay")}: ${delay}`,
480	+      ...(message ? [`${t("running_late_message_from_host")}: ${message}`] : []),
481	+    ];
482	+
483	+    return {
484	+      to: `${attendee.name} <${attendee.email}>`,
485	+      from: `${hostName} <${this.getMailerOptions().from}>`,
486	+      replyTo: hostEmail,
487	+      subject: t("running_late_subject", {
488	+        hostName,
489	+        eventTitle,
490	+        interpolation: { escapeValue: false },
491	+      }),
492	+      html: await renderEmail("AttendeeRunningLateEmail", {
493	+        hostName,
494	+        eventTitle,
495	+        originalStart,
496	+        delay,
497	+        message,
498	+        t,
499	+      }),
500	+      text: textLines.join("\n"),
501	+    };
502	+  }
503	+}

565	diff --git a/packages/features/bookings/lib/runningLate.test.ts b/packages/features/bookings/lib/runningLate.test.ts
566	new file mode 100644
567	--- /dev/null
568	+++ b/packages/features/bookings/lib/runningLate.test.ts
569	@@ -0,0 +1,43 @@
570	+import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
571	+import { isWithinRunningLateWindow, RUNNING_LATE_WINDOW_MS } from "./runningLate";
572	+
573	+const now = new Date("2026-11-12T12:00:00Z");
574	+const MINUTE = 60 * 1000;
575	+
576	+function meetingStartingIn(msFromNow: number, durationMs = 30 * MINUTE) {
577	+  const startTime = new Date(now.getTime() + msFromNow);
578	+  return { startTime, endTime: new Date(startTime.getTime() + durationMs), now };
579	+}
580	+
581	+describe("isWithinRunningLateWindow", () => {
582	+  it("allows a booking starting in 30 minutes", () => {
583	+    expect(isWithinRunningLateWindow(meetingStartingIn(30 * MINUTE))).toBe(true);
584	+  });
585	+
586	+  it("allows a booking starting exactly 2 hours from now", () => {
587	+    expect(isWithinRunningLateWindow(meetingStartingIn(RUNNING_LATE_WINDOW_MS))).toBe(true);
588	+  });
589	+
590	+  it("rejects a booking starting just over 2 hours from now", () => {
591	+    expect(isWithinRunningLateWindow(meetingStartingIn(RUNNING_LATE_WINDOW_MS + 1))).toBe(false);
592	+  });
593	+
594	+  it("allows a booking that is in progress", () => {
595	+    expect(isWithinRunningLateWindow(meetingStartingIn(-10 * MINUTE))).toBe(true);
596	+  });
597	+
598	+  it("rejects a booking at the exact moment it ends", () => {
599	+    expect(isWithinRunningLateWindow(meetingStartingIn(-30 * MINUTE))).toBe(false);
600	+  });
601	+
602	+  it("rejects a booking that has already ended", () => {
603	+    expect(isWithinRunningLateWindow(meetingStartingIn(-2 * 60 * MINUTE))).toBe(false);
604	+  });
605	+
606	+  it("accepts ISO strings as sent to the bookings list", () => {
607	+    const { startTime, endTime } = meetingStartingIn(15 * MINUTE);
608	+    expect(
609	+      isWithinRunningLateWindow({ startTime: startTime.toISOString(), endTime: endTime.toISOString(), now })
610	+    ).toBe(true);
611	+  });
612	+});
613	diff --git a/packages/features/bookings/lib/runningLate.ts b/packages/features/bookings/lib/runningLate.ts
614	new file mode 100644
615	--- /dev/null
616	+++ b/packages/features/bookings/lib/runningLate.ts
617	@@ -0,0 +1,26 @@
618	+export const RUNNING_LATE_DELAY_OPTIONS = [5, 10, 15, 30] as const;
619	+
620	+export type RunningLateDelayMinutes = (typeof RUNNING_LATE_DELAY_OPTIONS)[number];
621	+
622	+export const RUNNING_LATE_WINDOW_MS = 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
623	+
624	+export const RUNNING_LATE_MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH = 500;
625	+
626	+// Shared by the bookings list and the mutation so the button never shows for a booking the server would reject
627	+export function isWithinRunningLateWindow({
628	+  startTime,
629	+  endTime,
630	+  now = new Date(),
631	+}: {
632	+  startTime: Date | string;
633	+  endTime: Date | string;
634	+  now?: Date;
635	+}): boolean {
636	+  const nowMs = now.getTime();
637	+  const startMs = new Date(startTime).getTime();
638	+  const endMs = new Date(endTime).getTime();
639	+
640	+  if (nowMs >= endMs) return false;
641	+
642	+  return startMs - nowMs <= RUNNING_LATE_WINDOW_MS;
643	+}

894	new file mode 100644
895	--- /dev/null
896	+++ b/packages/features/bookings/services/RunningLateService.ts
897	@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@
898	+import AttendeeRunningLateEmail from "@calcom/emails/templates/attendee-running-late-email";
899	+import { getTranslation } from "@calcom/i18n/server";
900	+import { ErrorCode } from "@calcom/lib/errorCodes";
901	+import { ErrorWithCode } from "@calcom/lib/errors";
902	+import logger from "@calcom/lib/logger";
903	+import { BookingStatus } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";
904	+import { isWithinRunningLateWindow, type RunningLateDelayMinutes } from "../lib/runningLate";
905	+import type { BookingRepository } from "../repositories/BookingRepository";
906	+
907	+const log = logger.getSubLogger({ prefix: ["RunningLateService"] });
908	+
909	+export interface IRunningLateServiceDeps {
910	+  bookingRepository: BookingRepository;
911	+}
912	+
913	+export type SendRunningLateNoticeInput = {
914	+  bookingId: number;
915	+  userId: number;
916	+  delayMinutes: RunningLateDelayMinutes;
917	+  message?: string;
918	+  now?: Date;
919	+};
920	+
921	+export class RunningLateService {
922	+  constructor(private readonly deps: IRunningLateServiceDeps) {}
923	+
924	+  async sendNotice({
925	+    bookingId,
926	+    userId,
927	+    delayMinutes,
928	+    message,
929	+    now = new Date(),
930	+  }: SendRunningLateNoticeInput): Promise<{ sent: number }> {
931	+    const booking = await this.deps.bookingRepository.findByIdIncludeUserAndAttendeeTimeZones(bookingId);
932	+
933	+    if (!booking) {
934	+      throw new ErrorWithCode(ErrorCode.BookingNotFound, `Booking ${bookingId} not found`);
935	+    }
936	+
937	+    // Only the organizer may send: co-hosts and admins can see the booking but aren't the one running late
938	+    if (booking.userId !== userId || !booking.user) {
939	+      throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.Forbidden("Only the booking's host can send a running late notice");
940	+    }
941	+
942	+    if (booking.status !== BookingStatus.ACCEPTED) {
943	+      throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.BadRequest("Running late notices can only be sent for accepted bookings");
944	+    }
945	+
946	+    if (!isWithinRunningLateWindow({ startTime: booking.startTime, endTime: booking.endTime, now })) {
947	+      throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.BadRequest(
948	+        "Running late notices can only be sent within 2 hours of the start time or while the booking is in progress"
949	+      );
950	+    }
951	+
952	+    const host = booking.user;
953	+    const seenEmails = new Set<string>([host.email.toLowerCase()]);
954	+    const recipients = booking.attendees.filter((attendee) => {
955	+      const email = attendee.email.toLowerCase();
956	+      if (seenEmails.has(email)) return false;
957	+      seenEmails.add(email);
958	+      return true;
959	+    });
960	+
961	+    if (recipients.length === 0) return { sent: 0 };
962	+
963	+    const eventTitle = booking.title;
964	+    const trimmedMessage = message?.trim() || undefined;
965	+
966	+    const results = await Promise.allSettled(
967	+      recipients.map(async (attendee) => {
968	+        const locale = attendee.locale ?? "en";
969	+        const t = await getTranslation(locale, "common");
970	+        return new AttendeeRunningLateEmail({
971	+          attendee: { name: attendee.name, email: attendee.email, timeZone: attendee.timeZone, locale },
972	+          hostName: host.name ?? host.email,
973	+          hostEmail: host.email,
974	+          eventTitle,
975	+          startTime: booking.startTime,
976	+          delayMinutes,
977	+          message: trimmedMessage,
978	+          t,
979	+        }).sendEmail();
980	+      })
981	+    );
982	+
983	+    const failures = results.filter((result) => result.status === "rejected");
984	+    if (failures.length > 0) {
985	+      log.error(`Failed to send ${failures.length} running late email(s) for booking ${booking.uid}`, {
986	+        reasons: failures.map((failure) => String(failure.reason)),
987	+      });
988	+    }
989	+
990	+    return { sent: results.length - failures.length };
991	+  }
992	+}

```text
Sub-issue 1 of #131. Full feature spec: `specs/oidc-sign-in/` in PR #133. Numbers in brackets, such as [39], are acceptance criteria in `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md`.


### Is your proposal related to a problem?

#131 lets an admin add OIDC providers at run time. Today the only providers are hard-coded and configured with environment variables, and the database has no place to store a provider, its client secret, or its sign-up rules. `IdentityProvider` (`schema.prisma:367`) has no value for an OIDC user. Every other #131 sub-issue (admin backend, admin page, login flow) reads or writes this data, so it comes first.

### Describe the solution you would like

Add an `OIDC` value to `IdentityProvider` and a new `OidcProvider` table with a migration. Add `PrismaOidcProviderRepository`, wired with the moduleLoader DI pattern, that is the only code that reads or writes the table. It returns DTOs, never Prisma types. The client secret is stored only as ciphertext; encrypting it is the admin service's job (sub-issue 3), not the repository's.

### User story

As a developer on the #131 sub-issues, I want one repository for OIDC providers, so that the admin backend and the login flow read the same data in the same way and the secret cannot leak through a query that selects too much.

### User scenario

The admin service (sub-issue 3) calls `create` with an encrypted secret. The login route (sub-issue 5) calls `findEnabled` on each auth request and gets the enabled providers in display order, without their secrets, then calls `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret` for the one provider whose flow it builds. When an admin removes a provider, the service calls `deleteWithAccounts`, and the provider and every user link to it go in one transaction.

### Scope

Medium. It touches the Prisma schema and one migration, a new repository with its DTO, the DI module and container, and unit tests. I expect 6 to 8 files and about 300 changed lines, half of them tests. It adds no UI and no tRPC route.

### Acceptance criteria

1. A migration adds `OIDC` to `IdentityProvider` and creates `OidcProvider` with: `id` (cuid, primary key), `displayName` (text), `issuer` (text), `clientId` (text), `clientSecretEncrypted` (text), `scopes` (text), `allowSignup` (boolean), `allowedDomains` (text array), `enabled` (boolean), `position` (integer), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `updatedById` (nullable integer).
2. New rows get these defaults: `scopes = "openid email profile"`, `allowSignup = false`, `allowedDomains = []`, `enabled = false`, `position = 0`.
3. Two providers cannot have the same `issuer` and `clientId`. A second insert with the same pair fails with a unique-constraint error, and the repository turns it into an `ErrorWithCode` with a message that names the issuer, not the secret.
4. The migration applies to a database that already has users and accounts, and changes no existing row. `CAL`, `GOOGLE`, `SAML` and `AZUREAD` users keep their values. [39]
5. `findEnabled()` returns only enabled providers, ordered by `position` and then `createdAt`, as `OidcProviderPublicDto` (`id`, `displayName`, `issuer`, `clientId`, `scopes`, `allowSignup`, `allowedDomains`). It never selects `clientSecretEncrypted`. [6, 11]
6. `list()` returns every provider (enabled or not) in the same order and shape as criterion 5, plus `enabled`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. It never selects `clientSecretEncrypted`. [6]
7. `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret(id)` is the only method that returns `clientSecretEncrypted`. It returns `null` for an unknown id.
8. `create`, `update` and `setEnabled` write only the fields they are given. `update` without a new secret leaves `clientSecretEncrypted` unchanged. Each returns the shape of criterion 6.
9. `countLinkedAccounts(id)` returns the number of distinct users with an `Account` row whose `provider` is `oidc-<id>`. [36]
10. `deleteWithAccounts(id)` deletes the provider and every `Account` row with `provider = "oidc-<id>"` in one transaction. If either delete fails, neither happens. Deleting an unknown id throws `ErrorWithCode` not-found and deletes nothing. [37]
11. `getOidcProviderRepository()` returns the repository from the DI container, built with `bindModuleToClassOnToken` like `packages/features/credentials/di/CredentialRepository.module.ts`.
12. Every query uses `select`, never `include`. No method returns a Prisma type; the DTOs live in `packages/lib/dto/`.
13. `yarn type-check:ci --force` passes. Code that switches over `IdentityProvider` handles `OIDC` (for example the provider name on `/auth/error`, `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx:39-48`, falls back to "your original login method").
14. Unit tests with a mocked Prisma client cover criteria 3 and 5 to 10, including a check that the `select` of `findEnabled` and `list` has no `clientSecretEncrypted` key.

### Out of scope

- Encrypting or decrypting the secret, field validation, the 10-provider limit and the discovery test (sub-issue 3).
- Admin UI (sub-issue 4) and the login flow (sub-issue 5).
- Mapping `oidc-<id>` to `IdentityProvider.OIDC` in `identityProviders.ts` (sub-issue 5).
- Any change to `User` or `Account` columns. The user link is an `Account` row (ADR-002).

### Design decisions

**Where the provider order comes from.** Store an integer `position`, sorted with `createdAt` as the tie-breaker.

1. Sort by `createdAt` only. Rejected: the admin cannot put the main provider first (design criterion 11 asks for an admin-set order).
2. A linked list (`previousId`). Rejected: reordering needs several row updates and is easy to corrupt; 10 rows at most do not need it.

**How `allowedDomains` is stored.** A Postgres text array on the provider row.

1. A separate `OidcProviderDomain` table. Rejected: a second table and a join for at most a handful of strings that are always read with the provider.
2. One comma-separated text column. Rejected: the code must split and trim it everywhere, and a domain with a stray space would not match.

**How a user is linked to a provider.** Use the existing `Account` table with `provider = "oidc-<id>"`, not a new column on `User`. See ADR-002 in `specs/oidc-sign-in/decisions.md`: `Account` already has `@@unique([provider, providerAccountId])` (`schema.prisma:1258`), and a column on `User` would allow only one link per user.

**Who records the last editor.** `updatedById` is a plain nullable integer, not a relation to `User`.

1. A relation to `User`. Rejected: it changes the `User` model, which every Cal.diy query touches, for an audit field nobody joins on.
2. No editor field. Rejected: when two admins edit one provider (design criterion 8), the page cannot say who saved last.

### Technical notes

- Repository pattern: `packages/features/selectedSlots/repositories/PrismaSelectedSlotRepository.ts` (constructor takes `PrismaClient`).
- DI pattern: `packages/features/credentials/di/CredentialRepository.module.ts`; tokens in a new `packages/features/auth/oidc/di/tokens.ts`, spread into `packages/features/di/tokens.ts`.
- Migration folder name: `<timestamp>_add_oidc_provider` in `packages/prisma/migrations/`, after `20261029130000_add_waitlist_entry_slot_start`.
- Run `yarn prisma generate` after the schema change.
- Likely files: `schema.prisma`, the migration, `PrismaOidcProviderRepository.ts` and its test, `packages/lib/dto/OidcProviderDto.ts`, `OidcProviderRepository.module.ts`, `OidcProviderRepository.container.ts`, `tokens.ts` (two files), and `auth/error/page.tsx` if criterion 13 needs it.

### Mutation testing

The repository methods are short and have clear branches (unknown id, unchanged secret, transaction rollback), so StrykerJS can run on `PrismaOidcProviderRepository.ts` with only its own test file.
```

/** What the login flow may read about an enabled provider. It has no secret. */
export interface OidcProviderPublicDto {
  id: string;
  displayName: string;
  issuer: string;
  clientId: string;
  scopes: string;
  allowSignup: boolean;
  allowedDomains: string[];
}

/** What the admin list shows. It has no secret. */
export interface OidcProviderDto extends OidcProviderPublicDto {
  enabled: boolean;
  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
}

/** The only shape that carries the ciphertext of the client secret. */
export interface OidcProviderWithEncryptedSecretDto extends OidcProviderDto {
  clientSecretEncrypted: string;
}

export interface OidcProviderCreateDto {
  displayName: string;
  issuer: string;
  clientId: string;
  clientSecretEncrypted: string;
  scopes?: string;
  allowSignup?: boolean;
  allowedDomains?: string[];
  enabled?: boolean;
  position?: number;
  updatedById?: number | null;
}

export type OidcProviderUpdateDto = Partial<Omit<OidcProviderCreateDto, "enabled">>;

import { decodeHTML } from "entities";
import { z } from "zod";

import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
import { FeaturesRepository } from "@calcom/features/flags/features.repository";
import isSmsCalEmail from "@calcom/lib/isSmsCalEmail";
import { serverConfig } from "@calcom/lib/serverConfig";
import { getServerErrorFromUnknown } from "@calcom/lib/server/getServerErrorFromUnknown";
import { setTestEmail } from "@calcom/lib/testEmails";
import { prisma } from "@calcom/prisma";

import { sanitizeDisplayName } from "../lib/sanitizeDisplayName";

export default class BaseEmail {
  name = "";

  protected getTimezone() {
    return "";
  }

  protected getLocale(): string {
    return "";
  }

  protected getFormattedRecipientTime({ time, format }: { time: string; format: string }) {
    return dayjs(time).tz(this.getTimezone()).locale(this.getLocale()).format(format);
  }

  protected async getNodeMailerPayload(): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
    return {};
  }
  public async sendEmail() {
    const featuresRepository = new FeaturesRepository(prisma);
    const emailsDisabled = await featuresRepository.checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally("emails");
    /** If email kill switch exists and is active, we prevent emails being sent. */
    if (emailsDisabled) {
      console.warn("Skipped Sending Email due to active Kill Switch");
      return new Promise((r) => r("Skipped Sending Email due to active Kill Switch"));
    }

    if (process.env.INTEGRATION_TEST_MODE === "true") {
      // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment
      //@ts-expect-error
      setTestEmail(await this.getNodeMailerPayload());
      console.log(
        "Skipped Sending Email as process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_UNIT_TESTS is set. Emails are available in globalThis.testEmails"
      );
      return new Promise((r) => r("Skipped sendEmail for Unit Tests"));
    }

    const payload = await this.getNodeMailerPayload();

    const from = "from" in payload ? (payload.from as string) : "";
    const to = "to" in payload ? (payload.to as string) : "";

    if (isSmsCalEmail(to)) {
      console.log(`Skipped Sending Email to faux email: ${to}`);
      return new Promise((r) => r(`Skipped Sending Email to faux email: ${to}`));
    }

    const sanitizedFrom = sanitizeDisplayName(from);
    const sanitizedTo = sanitizeDisplayName(to);

    const parseSubject = z.string().safeParse(payload?.subject);
    const payloadWithUnEscapedSubject = {
      headers: this.getMailerOptions().headers,
      ...payload,
      ...{
        from: sanitizedFrom,
        to: sanitizedTo,
      },
      ...(parseSubject.success && { subject: decodeHTML(parseSubject.data) }),
    };
    const { createTransport } = await import("nodemailer");
    await new Promise((resolve, reject) =>
      createTransport(this.getMailerOptions().transport).sendMail(
        payloadWithUnEscapedSubject,
        (_err, info) => {
          if (_err) {
            const err = getServerErrorFromUnknown(_err);
            this.printNodeMailerError(err);
            reject(err);
          } else {
            resolve(info);
          }
        }
      )
    ).catch((e) =>
      console.error(
        "sendEmail",
        `from: ${"from" in payloadWithUnEscapedSubject ? payloadWithUnEscapedSubject.from : ""}`,
        `subject: ${"subject" in payloadWithUnEscapedSubject ? payloadWithUnEscapedSubject.subject : ""}`,
        e
      )
    );
    return new Promise((resolve) => resolve("send mail async"));
  }
  protected getMailerOptions() {
    return {
      transport: serverConfig.transport,
      from: serverConfig.from,
      headers: serverConfig.headers,
    };
  }
  protected printNodeMailerError(error: Error): void {
    /** Don't clog the logs with unsent emails in E2E */
    if (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E) return;
    console.error(`${this.name}_ERROR`, error);
  }
}

import type {
  OidcProviderCreateDto,
  OidcProviderDto,
  OidcProviderPublicDto,
  OidcProviderUpdateDto,
  OidcProviderWithEncryptedSecretDto,
} from "@calcom/lib/dto/OidcProviderDto";
import { ErrorWithCode } from "@calcom/lib/errors";
import type { PrismaClient } from "@calcom/prisma";
import { Prisma } from "@calcom/prisma/client";

const publicSelect = {
  id: true,
  displayName: true,
  issuer: true,
  clientId: true,
  scopes: true,
  allowSignup: true,
  allowedDomains: true,
} satisfies Prisma.OidcProviderSelect;

const adminSelect = {
  ...publicSelect,
  enabled: true,
  createdAt: true,
  updatedAt: true,
} satisfies Prisma.OidcProviderSelect;

const displayOrder: Prisma.OidcProviderOrderByWithRelationInput[] = [
  { position: "asc" },
  { createdAt: "asc" },
];

/** The value of `Account.provider` for a user linked to this provider (ADR-002). */
export function getOidcAccountProviderId(id: string): string {
  return `oidc-${id}`;
}

function isPrismaError(error: unknown, code: string): boolean {
  return error instanceof Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError && error.code === code;
}

export class PrismaOidcProviderRepository {
  constructor(private prismaClient: PrismaClient) {}

  async findEnabled(): Promise<OidcProviderPublicDto[]> {
    return this.prismaClient.oidcProvider.findMany({
      where: { enabled: true },
      orderBy: displayOrder,
      select: publicSelect,
    });
  }

  async list(): Promise<OidcProviderDto[]> {
    return this.prismaClient.oidcProvider.findMany({
      orderBy: displayOrder,
      select: adminSelect,
    });
  }

  async findByIdWithEncryptedSecret(id: string): Promise<OidcProviderWithEncryptedSecretDto | null> {
    return this.prismaClient.oidcProvider.findUnique({
      where: { id },
      select: { ...adminSelect, clientSecretEncrypted: true },
    });
  }

  async create(data: OidcProviderCreateDto): Promise<OidcProviderDto> {
    try {
      return await this.prismaClient.oidcProvider.create({ data, select: adminSelect });
    } catch (error) {
      throw this.toRepositoryError(error, { issuer: data.issuer });
    }
  }

  async update(id: string, data: OidcProviderUpdateDto): Promise<OidcProviderDto> {
    try {
      return await this.prismaClient.oidcProvider.update({ where: { id }, data, select: adminSelect });
    } catch (error) {
      throw this.toRepositoryError(error, { id, issuer: data.issuer });
    }
  }

  async setEnabled(id: string, enabled: boolean): Promise<OidcProviderDto> {
    try {
      return await this.prismaClient.oidcProvider.update({
        where: { id },
        data: { enabled },
        select: adminSelect,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw this.toRepositoryError(error, { id });
    }
  }

  async countLinkedAccounts(id: string): Promise<number> {
    // One user can hold two accounts at the same provider, so rows are not users.
    const users = await this.prismaClient.account.findMany({
      where: { provider: getOidcAccountProviderId(id) },
      distinct: ["userId"],
      select: { userId: true },
    });
    return users.length;
  }

  async deleteWithAccounts(id: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.prismaClient.$transaction(async (tx) => {
      const provider = await tx.oidcProvider.findUnique({ where: { id }, select: { id: true } });
      if (!provider) {
        throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.NotFound(`OIDC provider ${id} not found`);
      }
      await tx.account.deleteMany({ where: { provider: getOidcAccountProviderId(id) } });
      await tx.oidcProvider.delete({ where: { id } });
    });
  }

  // The message is built from the id and the issuer only. A Prisma error can print the
  // values of the failed write, and those include the ciphertext of the secret.
  private toRepositoryError(error: unknown, context: { id?: string; issuer?: string }): unknown {
    if (isPrismaError(error, "P2002")) {
      const issuer = context.issuer ? ` ${context.issuer}` : "";
      return ErrorWithCode.Factory.BadRequest(
        `An OIDC provider with the issuer${issuer} and this client ID already exists`
      );
    }
    if (isPrismaError(error, "P2025") && context.id) {
      return ErrorWithCode.Factory.NotFound(`OIDC provider ${context.id} not found`);
    }
    return error;
  }
}

=== 146
julissaehp
2026-11-13T04:04:12Z
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Sub-issue 6 of #131. Seed and criteria numbers come from `specs/oidc-sign-in/` in PR #133 (criteria 11, 12, 21–25 in `design.md`).

#131 lets an admin add OIDC providers, but users have no way to reach them: the login and sign-up pages only render the hard-coded Google and Microsoft buttons (`apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.tsx:198-230`, `apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx:632-734`).

Sign-in failures are also invisible today. When NextAuth cannot start or finish an OAuth flow, it redirects to `/auth/login?error=OAuthSignin` (or `OAuthCallback`, `AccessDenied`), but `login-view.tsx` never reads `error` from the URL (it only reads `callbackUrl` and `email`, `:140` and `:255`), so the user sees a normal login page with no explanation. This already affects Google and Microsoft sign-in, and it would affect every OIDC failure (provider down, wrong client secret, expired `state`). The `/auth/error` page also has no messages for the new OIDC error codes that sub-issue 5 will emit.

### Describe the solution you'd like

1. **Provider buttons.** The login page shows one "Continue with <display name>" button per enabled OIDC provider, in the admin's order, below Google and Microsoft. Clicking it calls `signIn("oidc-<id>")`. The sign-up page shows the same buttons only for providers with "allow new accounts" on, and none when sign-up is disabled site-wide. With no enabled provider, both pages look exactly as they do today. import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
import { getTranslation } from "@calcom/i18n/server";
import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";
import type { User } from "@calcom/prisma/client";

export const PASSWORD_RESET_EXPIRY_HOURS = 6;

const RECENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3;
const RECENT_PERIOD_IN_MINUTES = 5;

const createPasswordReset = async (email: string): Promise<string> => {
  const expiry = dayjs().add(PASSWORD_RESET_EXPIRY_HOURS, "hours").toDate();

  await prisma.resetPasswordRequest.updateMany({
    where: {
      email,
      expires: {
        gt: new Date(),
      },
    },
    data: {
      expires: new Date(),
    },
  });

  const createdResetPasswordRequest = await prisma.resetPasswordRequest.create({
    data: {
      email,
      expires: expiry,
    },
  });

  return `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL}/auth/forgot-password/${createdResetPasswordRequest.id}`;
};

const guardAgainstTooManyPasswordResets = async (email: string) => {
  const recentPasswordRequestsCount = await prisma.resetPasswordRequest.count({
    where: {
      email,
      createdAt: {
        gt: dayjs().subtract(RECENT_PERIOD_IN_MINUTES, "minutes").toDate(),
      },
    },
  });
  if (recentPasswordRequestsCount >= RECENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
    throw new Error("Too many password reset attempts. Please try again later.");
  }
};
const passwordResetRequest = async (user: Pick<User, "email" | "name" | "locale">) => {
  const { email } = user;
  const t = await getTranslation(user.locale ?? "en", "common");
  await guardAgainstTooManyPasswordResets(email);
  const resetLink = await createPasswordReset(email);
  const { sendPasswordResetEmail } = await import("@calcom/emails/auth-email-service");

  // send email in user language
  await sendPasswordResetEmail({
    language: t,
    user,
    resetLink,
