```typescript
});

describe("PrismaOidcProviderRepository", () => {
  describe("findEnabled (criterion 5)", () => {
    it("asks only for enabled providers, by position and then createdAt", async () => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.findMany.mockResolvedValue([]);

      await repository.findEnabled();

      const args = prismaMock.oidcProvider.findMany.mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(args.where).toEqual({ enabled: true });
      expect(args.orderBy).toEqual([{ position: "asc" }, { createdAt: "asc" }]);
    });

    it("selects the public fields and never the secret", async () => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.findMany.mockResolvedValue([]);

      await repository.findEnabled();

      const { select } = prismaMock.oidcProvider.findMany.mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(Object.keys(select).sort()).toEqual(
        ["allowSignup", "allowedDomains", "clientId", "displayName", "id", "issuer", "scopes"].sort()
      );
      expect(select).not.toHaveProperty("clientSecretEncrypted");
    });
  });

  describe("list (criterion 6)", () => {
    it("asks for every provider in the same order", async () => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.findMany.mockResolvedValue([adminRow]);

      const result = await repository.list();

      const args = prismaMock.oidcProvider.findMany.mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(args.where).toBeUndefined();
      expect(args.orderBy).toEqual([{ position: "asc" }, { createdAt: "asc" }]);
      expect(result).toEqual([adminRow]);
    });

    it("selects the public fields plus enabled, createdAt and updatedAt, and never the secret", async () => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.findMany.mockResolvedValue([]);

      await repository.list();

      const { select } = prismaMock.oidcProvider.findMany.mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(Object.keys(select).sort()).toEqual(
        [
          "allowSignup",
          "allowedDomains",
          "clientId",
          "createdAt",
          "displayName",
          "enabled",
          "id",
          "issuer",
          "scopes",
          "updatedAt",
        ].sort()
      );
      expect(select).not.toHaveProperty("clientSecretEncrypted");
    });
  });

  describe("findByIdWithEncryptedSecret (criterion 7)", () => {
    it("returns the ciphertext for a known id", async () => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.findUnique.mockResolvedValue({ ...adminRow, clientSecretEncrypted: CIPHERTEXT });

      const result = await repository.findByIdWithEncryptedSecret("prov_1");

      const args = prismaMock.oidcProvider.findUnique.mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(args.where).toEqual({ id: "prov_1" });
      expect(args.select.clientSecretEncrypted).toBe(true);
      expect(result?.clientSecretEncrypted).toBe(CIPHERTEXT);
    });

    it("returns null for an unknown id", async () => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.findUnique.mockResolvedValue(null);

      await expect(repository.findByIdWithEncryptedSecret("missing")).resolves.toBeNull();
    });
  });

  describe("create (criteria 3 and 8)", () => {
    const input = {
      displayName: "Keycloak",
      issuer: "https://idp.example.com/realms/cal",
      clientId: "cal-diy",
      clientSecretEncrypted: CIPHERTEXT,
    };

    it("writes only the fields it is given and returns no secret", async () => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.create.mockResolvedValue(adminRow);

      const result = await repository.create(input);

      const args = prismaMock.oidcProvider.create.mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(args.data).toEqual(input);
      expect(args.select).not.toHaveProperty("clientSecretEncrypted");
      expect(result).toEqual(adminRow);
    });

    it("turns a duplicate issuer and client ID into an error that names the issuer and not the secret", async () => {
      // Prisma prints the failed write in its message, so the raw error holds the ciphertext.
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.create.mockRejectedValue(
        prismaError("P2002", `Unique constraint failed. data: { clientSecretEncrypted: "${CIPHERTEXT}" }`)
      );

      const error = await repository.create(input).catch((e: unknown) => e);

      expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(ErrorWithCode);
      expect((error as ErrorWithCode).code).toBe(ErrorCode.BadRequest);
      expect((error as ErrorWithCode).message).toContain("https://idp.example.com/realms/cal");
      expect((error as ErrorWithCode).message).not.toContain(CIPHERTEXT);
    });

    it("passes an error that is not a unique-constraint error through unchanged", async () => {
      const dbDown = prismaError("P1001", "Can't reach database server");
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.create.mockRejectedValue(dbDown);

      await expect(repository.create(input)).rejects.toBe(dbDown);
    });
  });

  describe("update (criterion 8)", () => {
    it("leaves the secret unchanged when no new secret is given", async () => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.update.mockResolvedValue({ ...adminRow, displayName: "Company SSO" });

      await repository.update("prov_1", { displayName: "Company SSO" });

      const args = prismaMock.oidcProvider.update.mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(args.where).toEqual({ id: "prov_1" });
      expect(args.data).toEqual({ displayName: "Company SSO" });
      expect(args.data).not.toHaveProperty("clientSecretEncrypted");
      expect(args.select).not.toHaveProperty("clientSecretEncrypted");
    });

    it("writes a new secret when one is given", async () => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.update.mockResolvedValue(adminRow);

      await repository.update("prov_1", { clientSecretEncrypted: "iv:new-ciphertext" });

      expect(prismaMock.oidcProvider.update.mock.calls[0][0].data).toEqual({
        clientSecretEncrypted: "iv:new-ciphertext",
      });
    });

    it("turns a duplicate issuer and client ID into a BadRequest error", async () => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.update.mockRejectedValue(prismaError("P2002", "Unique constraint failed"));

      const error = await repository
        .update("prov_1", { issuer: "https://other.example.com" })
        .catch((e: unknown) => e);

      expect((error as ErrorWithCode).code).toBe(ErrorCode.BadRequest);
      expect((error as ErrorWithCode).message).toContain("https://other.example.com");
    });

    it("turns an unknown id into a NotFound error", async () => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.update.mockRejectedValue(prismaError("P2025", "Record to update not found"));

      const error = await repository.update("missing", { displayName: "x" }).catch((e: unknown) => e);

      expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(ErrorWithCode);
      expect((error as ErrorWithCode).code).toBe(ErrorCode.NotFound);
    });
  });

  describe("setEnabled (criterion 8)", () => {
    it.each([true, false])("writes only enabled = %s", async (enabled) => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.update.mockResolvedValue({ ...adminRow, enabled });

      const result = await repository.setEnabled("prov_1", enabled);

      const args = prismaMock.oidcProvider.update.mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(args.where).toEqual({ id: "prov_1" });
      expect(args.data).toEqual({ enabled });
      expect(args.select).not.toHaveProperty("clientSecretEncrypted");
      expect(result.enabled).toBe(enabled);
    });

    it("turns an unknown id into a NotFound error", async () => {
      prismaMock.oidcProvider.update.mockRejectedValue(prismaError("P2025", "Record to update not found"));

      const error = await repository.setEnabled("missing", true).catch((e: unknown) => e);

      expect((error as ErrorWithCode).code).toBe(ErrorCode.NotFound);
    });
  });

  describe("countLinkedAccounts (criterion 9)", () => {
    it("counts distinct users whose account provider is oidc-<id>", async () => {
      // The database applies `distinct`, so two rows back means two users.
      prismaMock.account.findMany.mockResolvedValue([{ userId: 7 }, { userId: 9 }]);

      const count = await repository.countLinkedAccounts("prov_1");

      const args = prismaMock.account.findMany.mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(args.where).toEqual({ provider: "oidc-prov_1" });
      expect(args.distinct).toEqual(["userId"]);
      expect(count).toBe(2);
    });

    it("returns 0 when no user is linked", async () => {
      prismaMock.account.findMany.mockResolvedValue([]);

      await expect(repository.countLinkedAccounts("prov_1")).resolves.toBe(0);
    });
  });

  describe("deleteWithAccounts (criterion 10)", () => {
    it("deletes the linked accounts and the provider inside one transaction", async () => {
      tx.oidcProvider.findUnique.mockResolvedValue({ id: "prov_1" });

      await repository.deleteWithAccounts("prov_1");

      expect(prismaMock.$transaction).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
      expect(tx.account.deleteMany).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ where: { provider: "oidc-prov_1" } });
      expect(tx.oidcProvider.delete).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ where: { id: "prov_1" } });
    });

    it("throws NotFound and deletes nothing for an unknown id", async () => {
      tx.oidcProvider.findUnique.mockResolvedValue(null);

      const error = await repository.deleteWithAccounts("missing").catch((e: unknown) => e);

      expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(ErrorWithCode);
      expect((error as ErrorWithCode).code).toBe(ErrorCode.NotFound);
      expect(tx.account.deleteMany).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      expect(tx.oidcProvider.delete).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it("rejects the transaction when the account delete fails, so the provider is kept", async () => {
      tx.oidcProvider.findUnique.mockResolvedValue({ id: "prov_1" });
      const failure = new Error("account delete failed");
      tx.account.deleteMany.mockRejectedValue(failure);

      await expect(repository.deleteWithAccounts("prov_1")).rejects.toBe(failure);
      expect(tx.oidcProvider.delete).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it("rejects the transaction when the provider delete fails", async () => {
      tx.oidcProvider.findUnique.mockResolvedValue({ id: "prov_1" });
      const failure = new Error("provider delete failed");
      tx.oidcProvider.delete.mockRejectedValue(failure);

      await expect(repository.deleteWithAccounts("prov_1")).rejects.toBe(failure);
    });
  });

  it("builds the account provider id as oidc-<id>", () => {
    expect(getOidcAccountProviderId("abc")).toBe("oidc-abc");
  });
});
```

```text
As a cal.diy administrator, I want to configure, validate, test, and manage OIDC identity providers so that users can securely authenticate through external identity providers without exposing sensitive credentials or enabling invalid configurations.

## User Scenario

## Scope

**Size:** Medium

This issue implements the OIDC admin provider service and tRPC procedures, including provider validation, client secret encryption, connection testing, provider management, authorization, and automated tests.

The estimated implementation is approximately 10–12 files and 550–700 changed lines, including tests.

To remain within the team's individual PR size limits, the implementation can be divided into two PRs:

- Provider configuration validation, client secret encryption, and discovery connection testing.
- Admin tRPC procedures, provider management, and repository integration.

The first PR can be implemented independently, while the second PR depends on the completion of #136.
```

```markdown
Sprint 3 review rubric for this PR, on head `4e95592ab2`.

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness: does the change do what the issue asked? | 7 | All four criteria are met in the code. The success toast can report emails as sent when SMTP failed (item 1), and the description and the code disagree about who counts as the host (item 2). |
| Test coverage: are tests present and meaningful? | 7 | 25 tests across `runningLate.test.ts`, `RunningLateService.test.ts` and `bookingActions.test.ts` cover the window edges, the organizer check, status and recipients. One test covers a failure path that the real email class does not produce (item 1). |
| Code quality: consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | 8 | It uses a repository method with `select`, DI like `BookingPeopleService`, `ErrorWithCode` in the service, and no `as any`. The window check is shared by the UI and the server. |
| Documentation: inline comments and PR description are clear | 5 | It has a design section and `Closes #137`. The title is not a conventional commit, and there is no Tech Debt section and no Test Evidence table. |

### Summary

This PR adds a "Running late" action to the booking actions menu. The host picks a delay of 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes and adds an optional message, and each attendee gets an email. The booking does not change. The tRPC mutation calls `RunningLateService`, which checks that the caller is the organizer, that the booking is `ACCEPTED`, and that it is in the window.

Spec check:

- Action only on accepted bookings within 2 hours or in progress: met. `bookingActions.ts:190-198`, `runningLate.ts:13-26`, enforced again at `RunningLateService.ts:45-53`.
- Delay of 5, 10, 15 or 30 and optional message: met. `runningLate.ts:1`, `runningLate.schema.ts:19-21`, `RunningLateDialog.tsx:61-110`.
- Every attendee gets an email with event, original start in their time zone, delay and message: met. `attendee-running-late-email.ts:27-41` uses the attendee's time zone and locale.
- Only the host can send, and the time does not change: met. `RunningLateService.ts:40-42` uses the session user id, and nothing writes to the booking.

### Changes requested

#### 1. The sent count counts failed emails as sent

`BaseEmail.sendEmail()` (`packages/emails/templates/_base-email.ts`) catches transport errors, logs them and resolves. It also resolves when the email kill switch is on. So in `RunningLateService.ts:69-93`, an SMTP failure is counted as sent. If the mail server is down, the host sees "Notified 2 attendees" and nobody gets an email. The test at `RunningLateService.test.ts:185` mocks `sendEmail` to reject, which the real class does not do for a send failure. Please change the toast to say that the notice was sent, without a delivery count, or say in the description that the count means "attempted".

#### 2. Say who the host is

The description says that a host is "the booking's organizer or one of its hosts". The code accepts only the organizer (`RunningLateService.ts:40-41`, `bookingActions.ts:190`). For collective events, the other hosts are stored as attendees (`createBooking.ts:157-159`), so they get the "X is running late" email (test at `RunningLateService.test.ts:114` expects this). Both choices are fine. Please make the description match the code and answer the "Team events" and "Notifying others" open questions from #137.

#### 3. Decide about repeat notices

Nothing limits how often a host can send. A host can send many emails to the same attendees during the window. #137 lists this as an open question. Please add a rate limit, for example `checkRateLimitAndThrowError` with an identifier per booking. If you do not, record it in a Tech Debt section.

#### 4. PR description and title

- Change the title to a conventional commit, for example `feat(bookings): add running late notice for hosts`.
- Add a Tech Debt section.
- Add a Test Evidence table with one row per acceptance criterion.

### Minor

- `RunningLateDialog.tsx:48` shows `error.message` in the toast. The service messages are English text, so other locales see untranslated errors. `t("unexpected_error_try_again")` or a mapped key would fix it.
- Without the AI log, the diff is about 876 lines in 20 code files (311 of them are tests). That is over the 500-line and 10-file guide in `CLAUDE.md`. A split into backend and UI was possible. I do not ask for it now, but please keep it in mind.
- The PR is not in draft mode. The repo rule is to open PRs as drafts.
```

```markdown
# Questions for the customer (#131)

Status: all 13 questions answered by `ojcchar` on #131 on 2026-11-12. The questions were posted on #131 by `zach-short` on 2026-11-11, in a shorter wording than the draft below; the numbers match. Each answer below is a summary of the customer's comment. Where an answer changed or added behaviour, the spec criteria named after "Spec" were changed or added (numbers in `design.md`).

Follow-up questions that the answers leave open are at the end of this file. They are not posted yet.

---

Hi @ojcchar, before we finish the spec for #131 we need your decision on the points below. For each one we give our proposal; please confirm it or tell us what you want instead. Q1 and Q2 block implementation.

**Blocking**

1. **Same email as an existing account.** Someone logs in with OIDC for the first time, and the provider says their verified email is `ana@uni.edu`. A Cal.diy account with `ana@uni.edu` already exists and is not linked to that provider. Any provider an admin adds can assert any email, so merging on email alone lets a misconfigured provider take over accounts. We propose:
   - (a) The admin lists the email domains each provider owns (for example `uni.edu`). A verified email in that list links to the existing account automatically.
   - (b) Any other match is rejected with a message telling the user to sign in their usual way and link the provider in Settings → Security.
   - (c) Accounts with the admin role never link automatically.

   Is this what you want? Or should every match be rejected (only (b)), or should every verified match link?

   **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** Agreed. Auto-link only when the email is verified and the admin marked the provider as owning that email domain. Otherwise reject, and the user links the provider from settings. Never auto-link an admin account. Spec: criteria 27, 27a, 3a; ADR-004, ADR-011.
2. **Who may create a new account through OIDC?** We propose a per-provider switch "allow new accounts" (off by default) and an optional list of allowed email domains. Is that right? Should the existing instance setting that disables sign-up also block OIDC sign-up?

   **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** Agreed on the per-provider switch (off by default) and the allowed domains. The global "disable signup" setting also blocks OIDC sign-up, and it wins over the provider switch. Invited users are the exception (Q8). Spec: criteria 12, 18, 18a.

**Need an answer this sprint**

3. **Providers that do not send `email_verified`.** Some providers leave out this claim. We propose to reject those logins (the #131 criterion), with no admin option to treat emails as verified. Do you agree?

   **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** Yes. Reject the login when `email_verified` is missing or false. Spec: criterion 15 (no change).
4. **Turning off password login.** Do you want a switch that disables password login when OIDC is set up? If yes, we propose that users with the admin role can always log in with a password, so no one can lock every admin out. We plan this for Sprint 4.

   **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** Yes, in Sprint 4. Admins always keep password login. Spec: criterion 41.
5. **Removing a provider.** When an admin removes a provider that users log in with, we propose: show how many users are linked and how many have no other login; require the admin to type the provider name; keep those users' accounts and data; and let them set a password with "Forgot password". Disabling a provider (hide it, keep links) is offered first. Is that right?

   **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** Fine, with two additions. Users created through OIDC have no password, so the team must prove that "Forgot password" works for them, with a test. Admins can also disable a provider in place of deleting it. Spec: criteria 36a, 37, 37a, 38.
6. **Two-factor authentication.** The site-wide "require 2FA" setting (#112) applies only to password users today. Should OIDC users also be forced to set up Cal.diy 2FA, or does their identity provider's MFA count?

   **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** Rely on the provider's MFA when it can be checked. Add a per-provider setting "accept this provider's MFA". When it is on and the ID token's `amr` claim shows a second factor, skip Cal.diy 2FA. When `amr` is missing or shows only a password, require Cal.diy 2FA. Sprint 4. Spec: criteria 3a, 44 to 47; ADR-010.
7. **Email changes at the provider.** A linked user's email changes at the provider. We propose to update the Cal.diy email at the next login if the new email is verified, not used by another account, and in the provider's allowed domains. Otherwise the login is rejected. Do you agree?

   **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** Fine, as long as accounts are matched by the provider's user ID (the `sub` claim), never by email. If the new email is already taken, keep the old email and tell the user. Spec: criteria 19 (no change), 31 (changed: the login is no longer rejected).
8. **Invited users.** An admin or team invited `bo@uni.edu`, who has not accepted yet. Should the first OIDC login with that email take over the invited account, or be treated like Q1?

   **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** A verified OIDC login with an invited email accepts the invite, even when "allow new accounts" is off for that provider. Spec: criterion 29 (changed), 18a.

**Can wait for Sprint 4**

9. **Groups to roles.** We propose that provider groups do not give Cal.diy roles in this feature (recorded as future work). Do you agree?

   **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** Agreed. No group mapping for now.
10. **Unlinking.** We propose that a user can unlink a provider in Settings → Security unless it is their only way to log in; then they must set a password first. Do you agree?

    **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** Agreed. Spec: criterion 35 (no change).
11. **Number of providers.** We propose up to 10 providers, shown on the login page in an order the admin sets. Is that enough?

    **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** Yes, 10 is enough. Spec: criterion 9 (no change).
12. **Test provider.** We will test against Keycloak running locally. Is Keycloak acceptable as the reference provider, or do you want us to test Authentik or Okta too?

    **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** Keycloak is fine. Document the setup so that anyone on the team can run the tests. Spec: criterion 42 (changed).
13. **Upgrade.** After the upgrade, nothing changes until an admin adds a provider. Downgrading after providers exist is not supported. Is that acceptable?

    **Answer (answered 2026-11-12):** Agreed. Spec: criteria 39, 40 (no change).

Thanks!

---

## Follow-up questions (not posted)

The answers leave these points open. Each has the team's proposal, which the spec uses until the customer answers. Post them on #131 as one comment after the team agrees.

- F1 (from Q8). Does an invite also skip the provider's allowed-domains list and the global "disable signup" setting? Proposed: yes to both, because the admin or team chose that exact email (criterion 18a).
- F2 (from Q8). Can an invite be accepted through auto-link when the invited email is on a domain the provider does not own? Proposed: yes, because criterion 29 needs only a verified email that equals the invited email.
- F3 (from Q6). "Require Cal.diy's 2FA" when `amr` shows no second factor: does it mean the TOTP step only for users who already set up 2FA, plus forced setup only when the site-wide "require 2FA" setting is on? Or does it force every such OIDC user to set up 2FA? Proposed: the first (criterion 46).
- F4 (from Q6). Which `amr` values count as a second factor? Proposed in ADR-010: `mfa`, or two or more different values with at least one that is not a knowledge factor.
- F5 (from Q7). If the new email at the provider is outside the provider's allowed domains, should Cal.diy keep the old email and tell the user, as for a taken email? Proposed: yes (criterion 31).
- F6 (not asked before). Should OIDC users join an organization by email domain? Proposed: no in this feature (criterion 32).

```

Cal.diy adds an `Account` row for (provider id, `sub`) to the invited user, sets `emailVerified`, the name (criterion 17) and a username, and handles the invite's team memberships the same way as an invited user who completes sign-up with the invite link. It does not use the L1021 code path (criterion 28). The invited user row is the one that existed; no second user is created. The allowed-domains list does not apply to an invite (proposal; follow-up F1 in `customer-questions.md`).""")
rep("""31. If another user has the new email, the login is rejected with `new-email-conflict` (existing message) and nothing changes.""",
```bash
"""31. A returning linked user whose email changed at the provider: the user is found by (provider id, `sub`) as in criterion 19, never by email. The new email and `email_verified` are read from the raw ID-token claims (`profile`), not from next-auth's `user` object, which holds the stored user once an `Account` row exists. If another user has the new email, or the new email is outside the allowed domains, the login succeeds, the user keeps the old email, and the next page shows a notice: "Your email at <display name> changed to <new email>, but that email is already used in Cal.diy. A new email with `email_verified` missing or `false` is rejected by criterion 15.""")

This holds while the provider exists and after it is removed. 44. A provider has the setting "accept this provider's MFA" (criterion 3a), default off. Only an admin can change it, on the provider form.
45. When the setting is on and the ID token's `amr` claim shows a second factor (ADR-010), the login skips the Cal.diy TOTP step, and the site-wide "require 2FA" setting (#112) does not ask that user to set up Cal.diy 2FA for that session. `amr` is read from the verified ID token only, never from userinfo.
46. When the setting is off, or `amr` is missing, empty, not a list of strings, or shows only a password, the login applies Cal.diy 2FA as for a password user: the TOTP step when the user has 2FA on (criterion 20), and the required-setup step when the site-wide "require 2FA" setting is on. This changes today's rule in `requiresTwoFactorSetup`, which exempts every non-`CAL` user (follow-up F3 in `customer-questions.md`).
```

```markdown
<!-- Draft PR body for branch feat/issue-136-oidc-provider-repository (local only, 2 commits on origin/main at 1ca2a73df1, head fad36d3efe). Written 2026-11-19. Not pushed, no PR opened. #136 has no spec-review comment yet; get one before you open this. -->

Title: `feat: add the OIDC provider table and repository (#136)`

Closes #136

## What this does

This is sub-issue 1 of #131. It adds the storage for OIDC providers that an admin adds at run time, and the one repository that reads and writes it. It adds no UI, no tRPC route and no change to the login flow, so nothing a user sees changes.

- `schema.prisma` and one migration: the `OIDC` value on `IdentityProvider`, and the `OidcProvider` table with a unique pair of `issuer` and `clientId`.
- `PrismaOidcProviderRepository` (`packages/features/auth/oidc/repositories/`): `findEnabled`, `list`, `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret`, `create`, `update`, `setEnabled`, `countLinkedAccounts`, `deleteWithAccounts`.
- DTOs in `packages/lib/dto/OidcProviderDto.ts`. No method returns a Prisma type.
- DI: `getOidcProviderRepository()` in `packages/features/auth/oidc/di/`, built with `bindModuleToClassOnToken`.

## Design

The design decisions are in #136 (provider order, `allowedDomains` as a text array, the `Account` row as the user link, `updatedById` as a plain integer), each with its rejected alternatives. Three choices were made during the build and are not in the issue:

**Which error code a duplicate gets.** `ErrorCode` has no conflict value. A duplicate `issuer` and `clientId` becomes `ErrorWithCode` with `BadRequest` (HTTP 400). Adding a `Conflict` code was rejected because it changes a shared enum and `getHttpStatusCode` for one caller. Passing the Prisma error through was rejected because Prisma can print the failed write in its message, and that write holds the ciphertext of the secret.

**How distinct users are counted.** `countLinkedAccounts` uses `findMany` with `distinct: ["userId"]`, because one user can hold two accounts at one provider and `count` would count rows. A `groupBy` gives the same number with a longer call.

**An unknown id on `update` and `setEnabled`.** #136 does not say. Prisma's `P2025` becomes `ErrorWithCode` `NotFound`, the same result that criterion 10 asks of `deleteWithAccounts`.

The migration SQL is the output of `prisma migrate diff` from the schema on `main` to the schema on this branch, unchanged.

## Tech Debt

- `deleteWithAccounts` reads the provider before it deletes, inside the transaction, so the unknown-id case costs one more query.
- The message for a duplicate on `update` names the issuer only when the update changes the issuer.
- The customer's answer on #131 (2026-11-12, question 6) asks for a per-provider "accept this provider's MFA" setting in Sprint 4. This table has no column for it. Sprint 4 needs a second migration.
- The customer's answer to question 1 speaks of the admin marking a provider as owning an email domain. This PR assumes `allowedDomains` holds that list. If sign-up domains and owned domains must differ, Sprint 4 needs another column.
- Biome reports 15 `nursery` infos (`useExplicitType`, `noTernary`) on the new files. The DI files they copy have the same infos.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1, AC2: table, columns and defaults | The migration equals `prisma migrate diff` output; columns and defaults read against the criterion text | manual | AC text |
| AC3: duplicate issuer and client ID fails with an `ErrorWithCode` that names the issuer, not the secret | "turns a duplicate issuer and client ID into an error that names the issuer and not the secret", "passes an error that is not a unique-constraint error through unchanged", and the `update` duplicate case | unit | AC text |
| AC4: the migration changes no existing row | Not run against a database here. The SQL only adds an enum value and creates a table | read | AC text |
| AC5: `findEnabled` returns enabled providers in order, without the secret | "asks only for enabled providers, by position and then createdAt", "selects the public fields and never the secret" | unit | AC text (field list) |
| AC6: `list` returns every provider with three more fields, without the secret | "asks for every provider in the same order", "selects the public fields plus enabled, createdAt and updatedAt, and never the secret" | unit | AC text (field list) |
| AC7: only `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret` returns the ciphertext; `null` for an unknown id | "returns the ciphertext for a known id", "returns null for an unknown id"; every other method asserts its `select` has no `clientSecretEncrypted` key | unit | AC text |
| AC8: `create`, `update`, `setEnabled` write only what they are given; no new secret leaves the secret unchanged | "writes only the fields it is given and returns no secret", "leaves the secret unchanged when no new secret is given", "writes a new secret when one is given", "writes only enabled = true/false" | unit | AC text |
| AC9: `countLinkedAccounts` counts distinct users with provider `oidc-<id>` | "counts distinct users whose account provider is oidc-<id>", "returns 0 when no user is linked" | unit | AC text |
| AC10: `deleteWithAccounts` is one transaction; unknown id throws not-found and deletes nothing | "deletes the linked accounts and the provider inside one transaction", "throws NotFound and deletes nothing for an unknown id", and the two "rejects the transaction when ... fails" cases | unit | AC text |
| AC11: `getOidcProviderRepository()` from the DI container | Type check only; no test loads the container | type check | AC text |
| AC12: `select` only, no Prisma type returned | Read of the repository; the DTOs are in `packages/lib/dto/` | read | AC text |
| AC13: type check passes with `OIDC` in the enum | `yarn type-check:ci --force`: 9 of 9 tasks. `/auth/error` already falls back to "your original login method", so it is not edited | type check | AC text |
| AC14: unit tests with a mocked Prisma client | 23 tests in `PrismaOidcProviderRepository.test.ts` | unit | AC text |

Gate results on this branch against `origin/main` at `1ca2a73df1`:

| Gate | Baseline | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| `yarn type-check:ci --force` | exit 0, 9 of 9 tasks | exit 0, 9 of 9 tasks |
| `TZ=UTC yarn test --exclude '**/.claude/**'` | 444 files and 4502 tests passed | 445 files and 4525 tests passed |
| `yarn biome check` on the changed files | n/a | 0 errors, 0 warnings, 15 infos |

### Not tested automatically, and why

- **The migration on a real database (AC4).** No Postgres ran on this machine. Run `yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-migrate` on a database with users before merge.
- **The unique constraint and the rollback in Postgres (AC3, AC10).** The tests use a mocked client, as #136 asks. They prove the repository calls one transaction and converts the error. They do not prove the database enforces either.
- **The DI container (AC11).** No test calls `getOidcProviderRepository()`.
- `yarn lint` for the whole repo and the `VITEST_MODE=timezone` suite did not run. No date code changed.

### AI-written tests

All 23 tests were written by an AI agent (Claude Code) together with the repository, not before it. Expected values come from the criterion text in #136: the field lists of criteria 5 and 6, the `oidc-<id>` form of criterion 9, and the error kinds of criteria 3 and 10.

### Mutation testing

Not run. #136 names `PrismaOidcProviderRepository.ts` as the target. The D6 run for this sprint was done on #130.

## Size

9 code files and 563 changed lines with the test file (307 lines). Without the test file: 8 files and 256 lines.
```

```text
    if (!booking) {
      throw new ErrorWithCode(ErrorCode.BookingNotFound, `Booking ${bookingId} not found`);
    }

    // Only the organizer may send: co-hosts and admins can see the booking but aren't the one running late
    if (booking.userId !== userId || !booking.user) {
      throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.Forbidden("Only the booking's host can send a running late notice");
    }

    if (booking.status !== BookingStatus.ACCEPTED) {
      throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.BadRequest("Running late notices can only be sent for accepted bookings");
    }

    if (!isWithinRunningLateWindow({ startTime: booking.startTime, endTime: booking.endTime, now })) {
      throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.BadRequest(
        "Running late notices can only be sent within 2 hours of the start time or while the booking is in progress"
      );
    }

    const host = booking.user;
    const seenEmails = new Set<string>([host.email.toLowerCase()]);
    const recipients = booking.attendees.filter((attendee) => {
      const email = attendee.email.toLowerCase();
      if (seenEmails.has(email)) return false;
      seenEmails.add(email);
      return true;
    });

    if (recipients.length === 0) return { sent: 0 };

    const eventTitle = booking.title;
    const trimmedMessage = message?.trim() || undefined;

    const results = await Promise.allSettled(
      recipients.map(async (attendee) => {
        const locale = attendee.locale ?? "en";
        const t = await getTranslation(locale, "common");
        return new AttendeeRunningLateEmail({
          attendee: { name: attendee.name, email: attendee.email, timeZone: attendee.timeZone, locale },
          hostName: host.name ?? host.email,
          hostEmail: host.email,
          eventTitle,
          startTime: booking.startTime,
          delayMinutes,
          message: trimmedMessage,
          t,
        }).sendEmail();
      })
    );

    const failures = results.filter((result) => result.status === "rejected");
    if (failures.length > 0) {
      log.error(`Failed to send ${failures.length} running late email(s) for booking ${booking.uid}`, {
        reasons: failures.map((failure) => String(failure.reason)),
      });
    }

    return { sent: results.length - failures.length };
  }
}
```

Commit: [PR #144](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/144/files) · Test: `packages/features/bookings/services/RunningLateService.test.ts` › keeps sending to other attendees when one email fails · Kills: `RunningLateService.ts:87` (`if (false)`)

## Questions

**1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**

The suriving mutants revealed that my tests checked what the code returned, but there was a gap in testing dependencies. There were two main blind spots in RunningLateService.test.ts:

1) sendNotice is the backend service method in RunningLateService that is run when the host clicks the Running Late button on a booking. It sends an email to each attendee of the event, records deliver errors in server logs, and return the number of emails that were succesfully sent. In my original code, the tests checked that sendNotice returned the message about how many successful emails were sent, but the tests did not check the server log errors. This means that if someone tried to break or delete the log later there would be no warning from the tests. 

2) The convention in this Cal codebase to translate text is to use the getTranslation function. This function nees two arguements: local (the attendee's langauge) and "common" (the namespace of what translation file to load). To test this, a mock helper was created so the test does not nee to load the real translation file from the disk. However, the fake function only accpeted the locale parameter and did not accept the namespace parameter. The gap is that the test was too forigving. The test passes on whatever namespace is, even if it is broken. 

**2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.**

# Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides

The Google connectors are thin wrappers over Google's raw APIs, with almost no guidance of their own. This skill supplies that guidance: which connector does what, the rules that keep edits in the user's file, and, in one reference file per app, how each API really behaves. Most of the app-specific rules in the references were tested against Google's Docs, Sheets and Slides APIs; the rest were seen through the connectors, and a few have not been checked yet.

## Read the reference before you touch the file

| Working on | Read first | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| A Google Doc | `references/docs.md` | Docs edits address UTF-16 positions that shift after every insert and go stale after every write. Tabs and pending suggestions change the positions too. |
| A Google Sheet | `references/sheets.md` | Both write tools parse input like the Sheets UI, so text can silently become numbers or dates. Formatting needs numeric sheet IDs, 0-based ranges, and field masks without parentheses. |
| A Google Slides deck | `references/slides.md` | Positions are in EMU, an element's real size is its size times its scale, and an unmasked read can exceed 150 KB for three slides. Slides never shrinks text to fit. |

Read the reference for every app the task touches before the first edit. Embedding a Sheets chart in a deck means reading both. The references are short, and skipping one is how edits land in the wrong place.

## 1. Check the connectors before you start

| Connector | What it can do |
|---|---|
| Google Drive | Create files, upload and convert content, rename, read a file as text, export (PDF and other formats), search, trash |
| Google Docs | Read a doc's full structure and edit it in place, directly or as suggestions |
| Google Sheets | Read values and structure, write values and formulas, format, add tabs and charts |
| Google Slides | Read a deck, add and edit slides, shapes, text, tables, and linked charts |

Drive can create all three file types. It can't edit a file after that. Without the matching editor connector, every change means a new file and a new link, and the user loses the link they already have.

1. Check which Google tools are available in this conversation. On surfaces where tools are deferred, search for and load the tools you need first, such as "google sheets update". Tool names differ by surface, so use the names your surface lists. If a search returns nothing, list all available tools before deciding the connector is missing, because the tool may exist under a different name.
2. If the editor tools are missing, tell the user. When you can list the conversation's connectors, say which case it is: a connector that is set up but turned off in this chat (ask them to turn it on in the chat's connector settings, then continue), or one that isn't connected at all (tell them which connector to add and what it enables).
3. With an editor connector missing, a request to create a new file continues with Drive. A change to an existing file stops and asks. See the missing-connector rule in section 2.
4. If the user asks only for a new file, create it with Drive. If the editor connector is off, add one line saying edits will need it.

Example: "I can create the sheet now. If you want changes later, turn on the Google Sheets connector in this chat first. Then I can edit this file, and the link will stay the same."

## 2. Rules for every file

- **A change goes in the same file.** "Change", "update", "fix", "add", and "switch it to" all mean the user wants the same file and link. Do not recreate the file to skip an edit.
- **A missing editor connector is a choice for the user, not a workaround for you.** When the user asks for a change to an existing file and the editor connector is missing, your whole reply is a short question, not a deliverable. Building the next-best thing feels helpful, but the user's file is still untouched and now there are two artifacts, which is the exact failure this skill exists to prevent. Lead with the fix: name the connector and say that with it on, the edit lands in their existing file and the link stays the same. You may offer an alternative, such as drafted text to paste or a file to import by hand, but only as a named option, and build it only after the user picks it. Example reply, in full: "To add the slide to your deck directly, turn on the Google Slides connector in this chat and I'll do it. Same deck, same link. Or I can draft the slide as a file you'd import by hand. Which do you prefer?"
- **Never trash a file the user didn't ask you to delete.** Drive can trash a file, but it can't restore one. The Docs, Sheets, and Slides connectors can't open a trashed file.
- **Read before you edit, and guard the write.** Send every Docs and Slides batch with `writeControl.requiredRevisionId` set to the `revisionId` from a read taken after your last write, including batches built on IDs or positions from your own earlier writes. The only exception is a batch made entirely of `replaceAllText` requests, even one limited to some tabs or slides. If the file changed since that read, whether from your own write or someone else's, Google rejects the whole batch instead of applying it at stale positions or IDs. Read again before each guarded batch, and don't reuse a revision ID from a write reply. On a rejection, read again and rebuild; never drop the guard. `read_doc` and `read_presentation` (the mask in `references/slides.md` includes it) return the ID. `read_slide_page` returns it only if its mask includes `revisionId`; `read_slide_page_thumbnail` and Drive `read_file_content` never do. For a saved read, the first line of `docs_index.py outline` or `slides_helper.py outline` shows it; if that line says `None`, read again with `read_doc` or `read_presentation`. `get_spreadsheet` doesn't return a `revisionId`, even when `fields` names it: send Sheets writes without `writeControl`, and read again right before a write that depends on positions.
- **Put everything for one step in one batch.** Batch requests run in order and atomically: if one is invalid, none apply. One call per logical step is faster and leaves no half-finished state.
- **Sheets field masks.** Write each path in full, with no parentheses: one path per item in `get_spreadsheet`'s `fields` list (`["spreadsheetId", "sheets.properties"]`), and comma-separated in a batch update request's `fields` string (`"userEnteredFormat.numberFormat,userEnteredFormat.textFormat.bold"`).
- **Verify the result.** Read the file again after each edit and check the result before you report it. A tool accepting the call does not mean the content is correct. Each reference has a Verify section.
- **Rename with Drive `update_file`.** A rename keeps the same link.
- **Link every file you name.** When you name a Google file you created, copied, found, or edited, make its title a link, inside the sentence that says what you did: "I added the row to [Team roster](its link)." Don't set the file apart after a colon or on a line of its own ("I've created a file for you: Team roster"). If a Drive result says the user can already see or open a file from the chat, leave that file's link out unless they ask. Always give the link when the user asks for it, wants to send it to someone, or says they can't see or open the file, even if a result said they could. Don't tell the user to use a card or preview unless a result said one is shown. After an edit, say that the link stays the same.

## 3. Drive, for all three apps

- **Find a file:** use Drive search when the user names a file without a link. Confirm the match with the user if more than one file fits. A page can be short even when more files match (5 files at page size 20) and can repeat the previous page's last file, so follow the next-page token until none comes back, and drop repeated ids.
- **Create:** `create_file` with `contentMimeType` set to `application/vnd.google-apps.document`, `.spreadsheet`, or `.presentation` creates an empty file. Uploading content with a source type (HTML, CSV, .xlsx, .pptx) converts it into the matching Google type. Each reference says which route fits that app.
- **Read as text:** `read_file_content` returns a compact text rendering: Markdown for a Doc. It is a few KB where the editor connector's full read can be over 100 KB, so use it to understand content, then use the editor read when you need positions. For a Doc, pass `includeComments: true`; without it, emoji come out garbled and the end of the text is cut off. For a Sheet, read the data with `get_values`: Drive returns only a sample (the first rows, long values cut).
- **Export:** `download_file_content` with `exportMimeType: "application/pdf"` returns the rendered file as base64. It is large (about 65 KB of text for a four-slide deck), so export only for a visual check, and only where you can run code.

## 4. Helper scripts

The `scripts/` folder next to this file holds tested helpers. They turn the APIs' raw JSON into short readable summaries, and turn simple specs into correct request batches, so the error-prone arithmetic never happens by hand. Use them wherever you can run Python. Run them by their full path inside this skill's folder; the references write that folder as `<skill>`.

| Script | Commands | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `docs_index.py` | `outline`, `find`, `new-table`, `fill-table` | Docs positions, text search with bold and suggestion state, adding a filled table in one call, filling an existing table |
| `sheets_helper.py` | `range`, `format`, `cells` | A1 ranges to grid ranges, formatting batches from a short spec, reading formulas and error cells |
| `slides_helper.py` | `outline`, `build` | Real slide geometry with overflow and overlap warnings, building slides from an inch-based spec |
| `render_export.py` | one command | Decoding a PDF export into page images to look at |

**Getting JSON to a script.** Large tool results are often saved to a file by the app, and the result tells you the path. Point the script at that path; the scripts read the file as the app saved it. When a result comes back in context and is small (a few KB, such as a masked read or sheet metadata), write it to a file and run the script on it. Don't re-type a large result into a file: that doubles the cost and invites copying errors. If a large result was cut off and not saved, read a smaller slice instead (a field mask, a range, or one tab) rather than guessing.

Every script prints `--help` with its full usage. Each reference shows the commands in context.

## 5. Common failures across apps

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "No such tool available" | The tool is deferred, or the name is different on this surface | Search for and load the tool. Use the exact name your surface lists. |
| Permission denied on a file you created | The file is in the trash | Ask the user to restore it from Drive's trash. You can't restore it with the connectors. |
| 400: required revision ID does not match | The file changed after your read: your own previous write, or someone else editing | Read again, rebuild the requests from the new read, and send them with the new revision. For Sheets, send them without `writeControl`. |
| A whole batch failed on one bad request | Batches are atomic | Fix the named request and resend the full batch. Nothing from the failed call was applied. |
| A read is too large or cut off | Unmasked editor reads include everything | Use Drive `read_file_content` (not for a Sheet), a field mask, a range, or a single tab. Run the helper on a saved result. |
| Two files where the user expected one | An edit was done by creating a new file | Make changes in place with the editor connector. Tell the user about the extra file; don't trash it without asking. |

Each reference ends with the failures specific to that app.

## 6. What the connectors can't do

When a request runs into one of these, say so plainly and do the alternative. *Reported*: seen through the connectors or in their tool schemas. *Untested*: not yet checked.

- **Claude can't see the user's screen.** No connector shows what the user has selected, or which file, tab or slide they have open. If "this" or "here" isn't clear from the chat, ask which file, heading, slide number or cell range they mean. *Reported.*
- **Comments:** `read_doc` with `commentsIncluded: true` has returned each comment with its place in the text. If the result shows `COMMENTS_VIEW_MODE_OMITTED` instead, use Drive `read_file_content` with `includeComments: true`, or ask the user to paste them. `update_doc` has accepted `insertComment` in one report, although its description is cut before listing it; if that request fails, say you can't add comments and offer to list your notes in the reply. *Reported.*
- **Suggestion mode can be refused** with "Unsupported WriteControl mode". Never make direct edits in its place: offer to list the proposed changes or to edit directly (see `references/docs.md`). *Reported.*
- **Request lists are cut short.** The `update_doc`, `update_spreadsheet` and `update_presentation` descriptions stop partway through their request lists. Requests missing from the description, such as `addDocumentTab` and `addChart`, have still worked, so try one before deciding it isn't supported. *Reported.*
- **Uploads travel inside the call.** `create_file` takes the whole file as text or base64, so an .xlsx or .pptx upload is slow and often fails. Build in the file with the editor connectors where you can, and keep uploads small. *Reported.*
- **Images need a public URL.** Slides `createImage` and Docs `insertInlineImage` fetch the image from a URL Google can reach; a file from the chat can't be inserted this way. For a deck, offer the .pptx route; otherwise ask the user to insert the image. *Untested.*
- **A Slides chart must already exist in a Sheet.** Create it there with `addChart`, then embed it with `createSheetsChart`. *Reported.*
- **Drive search uses `title`, not `name`.** `name contains '…'` fails with "Unsupported query field: name"; write `title contains '…'`, and put the file type in a `mimeType` clause. *Reported.*
- **Slides edits may not show in an open deck right away.** If the user doesn't see a change, ask them to reload the deck before you change anything again. *Reported; may be fixed.*
